{"parentUuid":"4701f19c-d0b9-42c2-85c2-91c3a350caf1","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"id":"call_5np4x5t8u5f9bujlfc39iw6l","input":{"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp8/b/src/io.rs","content":"//! Injectable I/O layer.\n//!\n//! All table reads and writes go through the two tiny traits in this module,\n//! which makes the storage backend replaceable in tests:\n//!\n//! * [`WritableFile`] — sequential, offset-free appends plus a durability\n//!   boundary (`sync_all`).\n//! * [`RandomAccessFile`] — reads at an absolute offset. Implementations are\n//!   free to return *fewer* bytes than requested (the table layer loops until\n//!   EOF), so short reads are normal behaviour and the fault injector uses\n//!   them to exercise that loop.\n//!\n//! Implementations provided here:\n//!\n//! * [`PosixWriter`] / [`PosixReader`] — real files via `std::fs`.\n//! * [`MemWriter`] / [`MemReader`] backed by a shared [`MemStore`] — fully\n//!   deterministic tables in memory.\n//! * [`FaultyWriter`] / [`FaultyReader`] — decorators injecting failures.\n\nuse std::fs::{File, OpenOptions};\nuse std::io::{Read, Seek, SeekFrom, Write};\nuse std::path::Path;\nuse std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};\nuse std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};\n\nuse crate::error::{Error, Result};\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Traits\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/// Sequential append-only sink.\n///\n/// `append` may perform a **short write**: it returns the number of bytes\n/// actually written (`0..=data.len()`). Callers must retry the remainder.\npub trait WritableFile {\n    /// Write as many leading bytes of `data` as possible.\n    fn append(&mut self, data: &[u8]) -> Result<usize>;\n    /// Flush data *and* metadata to stable storage. This is the table's single\n    /// durability boundary.\n    fn sync(&mut self) -> Result<()>;\n}\n\n/// Random read source; must be safe to share across threads.\npub trait RandomAccessFile: Sync {\n    /// Read into `buf` from absolute `offset`. A short read — including an\n    /// empty read at/after end of file — is `Ok(n)` with `n < buf.len()`.\n    fn read_at(&self, buf: &mut [u8], offset: u64) -> Result<usize>;\n}\n\n/// Honor [`WritableFile::append`] short writes with a retry loop.\npub fn append_all<W: WritableFile + ?Sized>(w: &mut W, mut data: &[u8]) -> Result<()> {\n    while !data.is_empty() {\n        let n = w.append(data)?;\n        if n == 0 {\n            return Err(Error::io_write(\"writer made no progress\"));\n        }\n        if n > data.len() {\n            return Err(Error::io_write(\"writer returned impossible byte count\"));\n        }\n        data = &data[n..];\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Loop until `buf` is filled or EOF reached; returns the number of bytes read.\n/// A return smaller than `buf.len()` means end of file.\npub fn read_fill<R: RandomAccessFile + ?Sized>(\n    r: &R,\n    buf: &mut [u8],\n    offset: u64,\n) -> Result<usize> {\n    let mut done = 0usize;\n    while done < buf.len() {\n        let n = r.read_at(&mut buf[done..], offset + done as u64)?;\n        if n == 0 {\n            break;\n        }\n        if n > buf.len() - done {\n            return Err(Error::io_read(\"reader returned too many bytes\"));\n        }\n        done += n;\n    }\n    Ok(done)\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// POSIX implementation\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/// Real on-disk writer. Created/truncated by [`PosixWriter::create`].\npub struct PosixWriter {\n    file: File,\n}\n\nimpl PosixWriter {\n    pub fn create(path: &Path) -> Result<PosixWriter> {\n        let file = OpenOptions::new()\n            .write(true)\n            .create_new(true)\n            .truncate(true)\n            .open(path)?;\n        Ok(PosixWriter { file })\n    }\n}\n\nimpl WritableFile for PosixWriter {\n    fn append(&mut self, data: &[u8]) -> Result<usize> {\n        Ok(self.file.write(data)?)\n    }\n    fn sync(&mut self) -> Result<()> {\n        Ok(self.file.sync_all()?)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Real on-disk random reader (a seek + read guarded by an internal mutex).\npub struct PosixReader {\n    file: Mutex<File>,\n}\n\nimpl PosixReader {\n    pub fn open(path: &Path) -> Result<PosixReader> {\n        let file = OpenOptions::new().read(true).open(path)?;\n        Ok(PosixReader {\n            file: Mutex::new(file),\n        })\n    }\n}\n\nimpl RandomAccessFile for PosixReader {\n    fn read_at(&self, buf: &mut [u8], offset: u64) -> Result<usize> {\n        let mut file = self.file.lock().expect(\"posix reader mutex poisoned\");\n        file.seek(SeekFrom::Start(offset))?;\n        Ok(file.read(buf)?)\n    }\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// In-memory implementation (test backend)\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/// A shared byte buffer. [`MemWriter`] appends; [`MemReader`] reads.\n#[derive(Clone)]\npub struct MemStore {\n    inner: Arc<Mutex<Vec<u8>>>,\n}\n\nimpl MemStore {\n    pub fn new() -> MemStore {\n        MemStore {\n            inner: Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::new())),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Snapshot of everything written.\n    pub fn snapshot(&self) -> Vec<u8> {\n        self.inner.lock().unwrap().clone()\n    }\n\n    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {\n        self.inner.lock().unwrap().len()\n    }\n\n    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {\n        self.len() == 0\n    }\n\n    /// Replace contents — used by corruption tests to mutate a stored file.\n    pub fn overwrite(&self, data: &[u8]) {\n        *self.inner.lock().unwrap() = data.to_vec();\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Default for MemStore {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        MemStore::new()\n    }\n}\n\npub struct MemWriter {\n    store: MemStore,\n    pos: usize,\n}\n\nimpl MemWriter {\n    pub fn new(store: MemStore) -> MemWriter {\n        MemWriter { store, pos: 0 }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl WritableFile for MemWriter {\n    fn append(&mut self, data: &[u8]) -> Result<usize> {\n        let mut buf = self.store.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        if self.pos != buf.len() {\n            return Err(Error::io_write(\"mem writer not positioned at end\"));\n        }\n        buf.extend_from_slice(data);\n        self.pos += data.len();\n        Ok(data.len())\n    }\n\n    fn sync(&mut self) -> Result<()> {\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\npub struct MemReader {\n    store: MemStore,\n}\n\nimpl MemReader {\n    pub fn new(store: MemStore) -> MemReader {\n        MemReader { store }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl RandomAccessFile for MemReader {\n    fn read_at(&self, buf: &mut [u8], offset: u64) -> Result<usize> {\n        let data = self.store.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        let start = offset as usize;\n        if start >= data.len() {\n            return Ok(0);\n        }\n        let end = (start + buf.len()).min(data.len());\n        buf[..end - start].copy_from_slice(&data[start..end]);\n        Ok(end - start)\n    }\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Fault injectors\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/// Failure script for [`FaultyWriter`].\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\npub struct WriteFaults {\n    /// The append call with this zero-based index fails with an IO error and\n    /// writes nothing.\n    pub fail_append_at: Option<u64>,\n    /// The append call with this index accepts at most this many bytes once\n    /// (clamped to a strictly short count), simulating a partial write.\n    pub short_write_at: Option<(u64, usize)>,\n    /// The sync call with this index fails.\n    pub fail_sync_at: Option<u64>,\n}\n\nimpl WriteFaults {\n    pub fn clean() -> Self {\n        WriteFaults::default()\n    }\n}\n\n/// Writer decorator that injects IO errors / short writes deterministically.\npub struct FaultyWriter<W> {\n    inner: W,\n    faults: WriteFaults,\n    appends: u64,\n    syncs: u64,\n}\n\nimpl<W: WritableFile> FaultyWriter<W> {\n    pub fn new(inner: W, faults: WriteFaults) -> FaultyWriter<W> {\n        FaultyWriter {\n            inner,\n            faults,\n            appends: 0,\n            syncs: 0,\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[allow(dead_code)]\n    pub fn append_calls(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.appends\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<W: WritableFile> WritableFile for FaultyWriter<W> {\n    fn append(&mut self, data: &[u8]) -> Result<usize> {\n        let call = self.appends;\n        self.appends += 1;\n        if self.faults.fail_append_at == Some(call) {\n            return Err(injected(\"write fault: injected append failure\"));\n        }\n        let n = self.inner.append(data)?;\n        if let Some((at, max_bytes)) = self.faults.short_write_at {\n            if at == call && !data.is_empty() {\n                // Guarantee a strictly short write.\n                let short = n.min(max_bytes).min(data.len() - 1);\n                return Ok(short);\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(n)\n    }\n\n    fn sync(&mut self) -> Result<()> {\n        let call = self.syncs;\n        self.syncs += 1;\n        if self.faults.fail_sync_at == Some(call) {\n            return Err(injected(\"write fault: injected sync failure\"));\n        }\n        self.inner.sync()\n    }\n}\n\n/// Failure script for [`FaultyReader`].\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\npub struct ReadFaults {\n    /// The read call with this zero-based index fails with an IO error.\n    pub fail_read_at_call: Option<u64>,\n    /// Every read returns at most this many bytes (fragmented IO).\n    pub max_bytes_per_read: Option<usize>,\n    /// Any read whose requested range contains this absolute offset stops one\n    /// byte short of it (a simulated device boundary), exactly once per call.\n    pub short_read_at_offset: Option<u64>,\n}\n\nimpl ReadFaults {\n    pub fn clean() -> Self {\n        ReadFaults::default()\n    }\n}\n\n/// Reader decorator injecting IO errors and short reads.\npub struct FaultyReader<R> {\n    inner: R,\n    faults: ReadFaults,\n    calls: AtomicU64,\n}\n\nimpl<R: RandomAccessFile> FaultyReader<R> {\n    pub fn new(inner: R, faults: ReadFaults) -> FaultyReader<R> {\n        FaultyReader {\n            inner,\n            faults,\n            calls: AtomicU64::new(0),\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[allow(dead_code)]\n    pub fn call_count(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.calls.load(Ordering::Relaxed)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<R: RandomAccessFile> RandomAccessFile for FaultyReader<R> {\n    fn read_at(&self, buf: &mut [u8], offset: u64) -> Result<usize> {\n        let call = self.calls.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);\n        if self.faults.fail_read_at_call == Some(call) {\n            return Err(injected(\"read fault: injected read failure\"));\n        }\n        let mut limit = buf.len();\n        if let Some(max) = self.faults.max_bytes_per_read {\n            limit = limit.min(max.max(1));\n        }\n        if let Some(point) = self.faults.short_read_at_offset {\n            // If the (already capped) range straddles `point`, stop just before\n            // it; always leave at least one byte for the retry loop to gather.\n            if offset < point && point < offset + limit as u64 {\n                limit = (point - offset) as usize;\n            }\n        }\n        self.inner.read_at(&mut buf[..limit], offset)\n    }\n}\n\nfn injected(msg: &str) -> Error {\n    Error::Io(std::io::Error::new(\n        std::io::ErrorKind::Other,\n        msg.to_string(),\n    ))\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn mem_write_read_roundtrip() {\n        let store = MemStore::new();\n        let mut w = MemWriter::new(store.clone());\n        append_all(&mut w, b\"hello world\").unwrap();\n        w.sync().unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(store.len(), 11);\n        let r = MemReader::new(store);\n        let mut buf = [0u8; 5];\n        assert_eq!(read_fill(&r, &mut buf, 6).unwrap(), 5);\n        assert_eq!(&buf, b\"world\");\n        let mut tail = [0u8; 8];\n        assert_eq!(read_fill(&r, &mut tail, 8).unwrap(), 3);\n        assert_eq!(&tail[..3], b\"rld\");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn faulty_writer_append_error() {\n        let store = MemStore::new();\n        let mut w = FaultyWriter::new(\n            MemWriter::new(store),\n            WriteFaults {\n                fail_append_at: Some(1),\n                ..WriteFaults::default()\n            },\n        );\n        assert!(w.append(b\"a\").is_ok());\n        assert!(w.append(b\"b\").is_err());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn faulty_writer_short_write_is_retried_by_append_all() {\n        let store = MemStore::new();\n        let mut w = FaultyWriter::new(\n            MemWriter::new(store.clone()),\n            WriteFaults {\n                short_write_at: Some((0, 2)),\n                ..WriteFaults::default()\n            },\n        );\n        append_all(&mut w, b\"abcdef\").unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(store.snapshot(), b\"abcdef\");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn faulty_writer_sync_error() {\n        let store = MemStore::new();\n        let mut w = FaultyWriter::new(\n            MemWriter::new(store),\n            WriteFaults {\n                fail_sync_at: Some(0),\n                ..WriteFaults::default()\n            },\n        );\n        assert!(w.sync().is_err());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn faulty_reader_fragmented_reads_still_assemble() {\n MemReader::new(store),\n            ReadFaults {\n                max_bytes_per_read: Some(3),\n                ..ReadFaults::default()\n            },\n        );\n        let mut buf = [0u8; 10];\n        assert_eq!(read_fill(&r, &mut buf, 0).unwrap(), 10);\n        assert_eq!(&buf, b\"abcdefghij\");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn faulty_reader_injected_error() {\n        let store = MemStore::new();\n        let mut w = MemWriter::new(store.clone());\n        append_all(&mut w, b\"abcdefghij\").unwrap();\n        let r = FaultyReader::new(\n            MemReader::new(store),\n buf, 0).is_ok());\n        assert!(r.read_at(&mut buf, 4).is_err());\n Implementations provided here:\n//!\n//! * [`PosixWriter`] / [`PosixReader`] — real files via `std::fs`.\n//! * [`MemWriter`] / [`MemReader`] backed by a shared [`MemStore`] — fully\n//!   deterministic tables in memory.\n//! * [`FaultyWriter`] / [`FaultyReader`] — decorators injecting failures.\n\nuse std::fs::{File, OpenOptions};\nuse std::io::{Read, Seek, SeekFrom, Write};\nuse std::path::Path;\nuse std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};\nuse std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};\n\nuse crate::error::{Error, Result};\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Traits\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/// Sequential append-only sink.\n///\n/// `append` may perform a **short write**: it returns the number of bytes\n/// actually written (`0..=data.len()`). Callers must retry the remainder.\npub trait WritableFile {\n    /// Write as many leading bytes of `data` as possible.\n    fn append(&mut self, data: &[u8]) -> Result<usize>;\n    /// Flush data *and* metadata to stable storage. This is the table's single\n    /// durability boundary.\n    fn sync(&mut self) -> Result<()>;\n}\n\n/// Random read source; must be safe to share across threads.\npub trait RandomAccessFile: Sync {\n    /// Read into `buf` from absolute `offset`. A short read — including an\n    /// empty read at/after end of file — is `Ok(n)` with `n < buf.len()`.\n    fn read_at(&self, buf: &mut [u8], offset: u64) -> Result<usize>;\n}\n\n/// Honor [`WritableFile::append`] short writes with a retry loop.\npub fn append_all<W: WritableFile + ?Sized>(w: &mut W, mut data: &[u8]) -> Result<()> {\n    while !data.is_empty() {\n        let n = w.append(data)?;\n        if n == 0 {\n            return Err(Error::io_write(\"writer made no progress\"));\n        }\n        if n > data.len() {\n            return Err(Error::io_write(\"writer returned impossible byte count\"));\n        }\n        data = &data[n..];\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Loop until `buf` is filled or EOF reached; returns the number of bytes read.\n/// A return smaller than `buf.len()` means end of file.\npub fn read_fill<R: RandomAccessFile + ?Sized>(\n    r: &R,\n    buf: &mut [u8],\n    offset: u64,\n) -> Result<usize> {\n    let mut done = 0usize;\n    while done < buf.len() {\n        let n = r.read_at(&mut buf[done..], offset + done as u64)?;\n        if n == 0 {\n            break;\n        }\n        if n > buf.len() - done {\n            return Err(Error::io_read(\"reader returned too many bytes\"));\n        }\n        done += n;\n    }\n    Ok(done)\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// POSIX implementation\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/// Real on-disk writer. Created/truncated by [`PosixWriter::create`].\npub struct PosixWriter {\n    file: File,\n}\n\nimpl PosixWriter {\n    pub fn create(path: &Path) -> Result<PosixWriter> {\n        let file = OpenOptions::new()\n            .write(true)\n            .create_new(true)\n            .truncate(true)\n            .open(path)?;\n        Ok(PosixWriter { file })\n    }\n}\n\nimpl WritableFile for PosixWriter {\n    fn append(&mut self, data: &[u8]) -> Result<usize> {\n        Ok(self.file.write(data)?)\n    }\n    fn sync(&mut self) -> Result<()> {\n        Ok(self.file.sync_all()?)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Real on-disk random reader (a seek + read guarded by an internal mutex).\npub struct PosixReader {\n    file: Mutex<File>,\n}\n\nimpl PosixReader {\n    pub fn open(path: &Path) -> Result<PosixReader> {\n        let file = OpenOptions::new().read(true).open(path)?;\n        Ok(PosixReader {\n            file: Mutex::new(file),\n        })\n    }\n}\n\nimpl RandomAccessFile for PosixReader {\n    fn read_at(&self, buf: &mut [u8], offset: u64) -> Result<usize> {\n        let mut file = self.file.lock().expect(\"posix reader mutex poisoned\");\n        file.seek(SeekFrom::Start(offset))?;\n        Ok(file.read(buf)?)\n    }\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// In-memory implementation (test backend)\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/// A shared byte buffer. See the [`crate::format`] module documentation for the byte-level layout.\n\nuse crate::coding;\nuse crate::error::{Error, Result};\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Write side\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/// Builds one data or index block in memory.\npub struct BlockBuilder {\n    buf: Vec<u8>,\n    restarts: Vec<u32>,\n    last_key: Vec<u8>,\n    counter: u32,\n    restart_interval: u32,\n}\n\nimpl BlockBuilder {\n    /// `restart_interval` is the number of entries between restart points;\n    /// every entry at an index divisible by it stores a full (uncompressed)\n    /// key. Must be at least 1; index blocks use 1.\n    pub fn new(restart_interval: u32) -> Result<BlockBuilder> {\n        if restart_interval == 0 {\n            return Err(Error::invalid_argument(\"restart_interval must be >= 1\"));\n        }\n        Ok(BlockBuilder {\n            buf: Vec::new(),\n            restarts: Vec::new(),\n            last_key: Vec::new(),\n            counter: 0,\n            restart_interval,\n        })\n    }\n\n    pub fn reset(&mut self) {\n        self.buf.clear();\n        self.restarts.clear();\n        self.last_key.clear();\n        self.counter = 0;\n    }\n\n    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {\n        self.counter == 0 && self.restarts.is_empty()\n    }\n\n    /// Entries buffered since the last restart point (LevelDB's `counter`).\n    pub fn entries_since_restart(&self) -> u32 {\n        self.counter\n    }\n\n    /// Current encoded size including the restart array that will be appended.\n    pub fn estimated_size(&self) -> usize {\n        self.buf.len() + self.restarts.len() * 4 + 4\n    }\n\n    /// Append a key/value pair. Keys MUST be strictly increasing; the builder\n    /// itself does not check (the table layer does).\n    pub fn add(&mut self, key: &[u8], value: &[u8]) {\n        let restart = self.counter >= self.restart_interval;\n        let shared = if restart {\n            self.restarts.push(self.buf.len() as u32);\n            self.counter = 0;\n            0usize\n        } else {\n            common_prefix(&self.last_key, key)\n        };\n\n        // Strictly increasing keys guarantee shared < key.len(); an empty key\n        // is legal as the very first (restart) entry.\n        debug_assert!(restart || shared < key.len());\n\n        let non_shared = key.len() - shared;\n        coding::put_varint32(&mut self.buf, shared as u32);\n        coding::put_varint32(&mut self.buf, non_shared as u32);\n        coding::put_varint32(&mut self.buf, value.len() as u32);\n        self.buf.extend_from_slice(&key[shared..]);\n        self.buf.extend_from_slice(value);\n\n        self.last_key.truncate(shared);\n        self.last_key.extend_from_slice(&key[shared..]);\n        self.counter += 1;\n    }\n\n    /// Append the restart array and return the finished payload. The builder is\n    /// left in an unusable-until-[`BlockBuilder::reset`] state.\n    pub fn finish(&mut self) -> &[u8] {\n        for r in &self.restarts {\n            coding::put_u32_le(&mut self.buf, *r);\n        }\n        coding::put_u32_le(&mut self.buf, self.restarts.len() as u32);\n        &self.buf\n    }\n}\n\n/// Length of the longest common prefix of `a` and `b`.\npub fn common_prefix(a: &[u8], b: &[u8]) -> usize {\n    let mut i = 0;\n    let max = a.len().min(b.len());\n    while i < max && a[i] == b[i] {\n        i += 1;\n    }\n    i\n}\n\n// /// Parse and structurally validate the restart array of a payload.\n    pub fn parse(data: Vec<u8>) -> Result<Block> {\n        if data.len() < 4 {\n            return offset {off} points at/after restart array\"\n                )));\n            }\n            match prev {\n                None => {\n                    if off != 0 {\n                        return Err(Error::corruption(\n                            \"first restart point must be at offset 0\",\n                        ));\n                    }\n                }\n                Some(p) target.as_ref_bytes() {\n                lo = mid;\n            } else {\n                hi = mid - 1;\n            }\n        }\n\n        let mut cur = Cursor::new(self);\n        cur.seek_to_restart_point(lo as usize);\n        while cur.next()? {\n            if cur.key.as_slice() >= target {\n                return Ok(cur);\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(cur) // exhausted\n    }\n}\n\n/// Helper trait so `&[u8]` comparisons above read naturally.\ntrait AsRefBytes {\n    fn as_ref_bytes(&self) -> &[u8];\n}\nimpl AsRefBytes for [u8] {\n    fn as_ref_bytes(&self) -> &[u8] {\n        self\n    }\n}\n\n/// Sanity ceiling on restart points in a single block (16M).\nconst MAX_RESTARTS: u32 = 1 << 24;\n\n/// Decoded header/locations of one block entry.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct EntryHeader {\n    pub shared: u32,\n    pub non_shared: u32,\n    pub value_len: u32,\n    pub key_delta_offset: usize,\n    pub value_offset: usize,\n    pub next_offset: usize,\n}\n\nimpl EntryHeader {\n    fn decode(data: &[u8], pos: usize, end: usize) -> Result<EntryHeader> {\n        let (shared, n1) = coding::decode_varint32(data, pos)?;\n        let (non_shared, n2) = coding::decode_varint32(data, pos + n1)?;\n        let (value_len, n3) = coding::decode_varint32(data, pos + n1 + n2)?;\n        let key_delta_offset = pos + n1 + n2 + n3;\n value_offset\n            .checked_add(value_len as usize)\n            .ok_or_else(|| Error::corruption(\"entry value length overflow\"))?;\n        if next_offset > end {\n            return Err(Error::corruption(\"entry overruns into restart array\"));\n        }\n        Ok(EntryHeader {\n            shared,\n            non_shared,\n            value_len,\n            key_delta_offset,\n            value_offset,\n            next_offset,\n        })\n    }\n\n    pub fn value_range(&self) -> (usize, usize) {\n        (self.value_offset, self.value_offset + self.value_len as usize)\n    }\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Cursor\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/// Forward cursor over a [`Block`]. Key reconstruction state is owned here.\npub struct Cursor<'a> {\n    block: &'a Block,\n    pos: usize,\n    valid: bool,\n    key: Vec<u8>,\n}\n\nimpl<'a> Cursor<'a> {\n    fn new(block: &'a Block) -> Cursor<'a> {\n        Cursor {\n            block,\n            pos: 0,\n            valid: false,\n            key: Vec::new(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn seek_to_restart_point(&mut self, index: usize) {\n        self.key.clear();\n        self.pos = self.block.restart_point(index);\n        self.valid = false;\n    }\n\n    fn seek_to_first(&mut self) {\n        self.seek_to_restart_point(0);\n    }\n\n    /// Advance to the next entry; returns `false` at end of block.\n    pub fn next(&mut self) -> Result<bool> {\n        if self.pos >= self.block.restart_offset {\n            self.valid = false;\n            return Ok(false);\n        }\n        let h = self.block.entry_at(self.pos)?;\n        if h.shared as usize > self.key.len() {\n            return Err(Error::corruption(format!(\n                \"entry at {} shares {} bytes but previous key is {} bytes\",\n                self.pos,\n                h.shared,\n                self.key.len()\n            )));\n        }\n        self.key.truncate(h.shared as usize);\n        self.key.extend_from_slice(\n            &self.block.data\n                [h.key_delta_offset..h.key_delta_offset + h.non_shared as usize],\n        );\n        self.pos = h.next_offset;\n        self.valid = true;\n        Ok(true)\n    }\n\n    pub fn valid(&self) -> bool {\n        self.valid\n    }\n\n    pub fn key(&self) -> &[u8] {\n        &self.key\n    }\n\n    /// Value bytes of the current entry (borrowed from the block).\n    pub fn value(&self) -> Result<&'a [u8]> {\n        let h = self.block.entry_at(self.previous_offset())?;\n        Ok(&self.block.data[h.value_offset..h.value_offset + h.value_len as usize])\n    }\n\n    /// Offset of the entry currently pointed at (position before advancing).\n    fn previous_offset(&self) -> usize {\n        // Recompute cheaply: value() callers already decoded via next(); Must be at least 1; index blocks use 1.\n    pub fn new(restart_interval: u32) -> Result<BlockBuilder> {\n        if restart_interval == 0 {\n            return Err(Error::invalid_argument(\"restart_interval must be >= 1\"));\n        }\n        Ok(BlockBuilder {\n            buf: Vec::new(),\n            restarts: Vec::new(),\n            last_key: Vec::new(),\n            counter: 0,\n            restart_interval,\n        })\n    }\n\n    pub fn reset(&mut self) {\n        self.buf.clear();\n        self.restarts.clear();\n        self.last_key.clear();\n        self.counter = 0;\n    }\n\n    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {\n        self.restarts.is_empty()\n    }\n\n    /// Entries buffered since the last restart point.\n    pub fn entries_since_restart(&self) -> u32 {\n        self.counter\n    }\n\n    /// Current encoded size including the restart array that will be appended.\n    pub fn estimated_size(&self) -> usize {\n        self.buf.len() + self.restarts.len() * 4 + 4\n    }\n\n    /// Append a key/value pair. Keys MUST be strictly increasing; the builder\n    /// itself does not check (the table layer does).\n    pub fn add(&mut self, key: &[u8], value: &[u8]) {\n        let restart = self.counter >= self.restart_interval;\n        let shared = if restart {\n            self.restarts.push(self.buf.len() as u32);\n            self.counter = 0;\n            0usize\n        } else {\n            common_prefix(&self.last_key, key)\n        };\n\n        // Strictly increasing keys guarantee shared < key.len(); an empty key\n        // is legal as the very first (restart) entry.\n        debug_assert!(restart || shared < key.len());\n\n        let non_shared = key.len() - shared;\n        coding::put_varint32(&mut self.buf, shared as u32);\n        coding::put_varint32(&mut self.buf, non_shared as u32);\n        coding::put_varint32(&mut self.buf, value.len() as u32);\n        self.buf.extend_from_slice(&key[shared..]);\n        self.buf.extend_from_slice(value);\n\n        self.last_key.truncate(shared);\n        self.last_key.extend_from_slice(&key[shared..]);\n        self.counter += 1;\n    }\n\n    /// Append the restart array and return the finished payload. Call\n    /// [`BlockBuilder::reset`] before reusing the builder afterwards.\n    pub fn finish(&mut self) -> &[u8] {\n        for r in &self.restarts {\n            coding::put_u32_le(&mut self.buf, *r);\n        }\n        coding::put_u32_le(&mut self.buf, self.restarts.len() as u32);\n        &self.buf\n    }\n}\n\n/// Length of the longest common prefix of `a` and `b`.\npub fn common_prefix(a: &[u8], b: &[u8]) -> usize {\n    let mut i = 0;\n    let max = a.len().min(b.len());\n    while i < max && a[i] == b[i] {\n        i += 1;\n    }\n    i\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Read side: parsed block\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/// A parsed, immutable block payload (trailer already stripped and verified).\n#[derive(Clone)]\npub struct Block {\n    data: Vec<u8>,\n    restart_offset: usize,\n    num_restarts: u32,\n}\n\n/// Sanity ceiling on restart points in a single block (16M).\nconst MAX_RESTARTS: u32 = 1 << 24;\n\nimpl Block {\n    /// Parse a payload and structurally validate the restart array.\n    pub fn parse(data: Vec<u8>) -> Result<Block> {\n        if data.len() < 4 {\n            return Err(Error::corruption(format!(\n                \"block payload too short for restart count: {} bytes\",\n                data.len()\n            )));\n        }\n        let num_restarts = coding::decode_u32_le(&data[data.len() - 4..]);\n        let array_bytes = (num_restarts as u64)\n            .checked_mul(4)\n            .ok_or_else(|| Error::corruption(\"restart count overflow\"))?\n            as usize;\n        if array_bytes + 4 > data.len() {\n            return Err(Error::corruption(\"restart array overruns block\"));\n        }\n        let restart_offset = data.len() - 4 - array_bytes;\n\n        if num_restarts == 0 {\n            return Err(Error::corruption(\"block has zero restart points\"));\n        }\n        if num_restarts > MAX_RESTARTS {\n            return Err(Error::corruption(\"restart count absurdly large\"));\n        }\n\n        let mut prev: Option<u32> = None;\n        for i in 0..num_restarts as usize {\n            let off = coding::decode_u32_le(&data[restart_offset + i * 4..]);\n            if (off as usize) >= restart_offset {\n                return Err(Error::corruption(format!(\n                    \"restart[{i}] offset {off} points at/after restart array\"\n                )));\n            }\n            match prev {\n                None => {\n                    if off != 0 {\n                        return Err(Error::corruption(\n                            \"first restart point must be at offset 0\",\n                        ));\n                    }\n                }\n                Some(p) if off <= p => {\n                    return Err(Error::corruption(\n                        \"restart offsets must be strictly increasing\",\n                    ));\n                }\n                Some(_) => {}\n            }\n            prev = Some(off);\n        }\n\n        Ok(Block {\n            data,\n            restart_offset,\n            num_restarts,\n        })\n    }\n\n    pub fn num_restarts(&self) -> usize {\n        self.num_restarts as usize\n    }\n\n    pub fn restart_offset(&self) -> usize {\n        self.restart_offset\n    }\n\n    pub fn payload(&self) -> &[u8] {\n        &self.data\n    }\n\n    /// Offset recorded by restart point `i`.\n    pub fn restart_point(&self, i: usize) -> usize {\n        coding::decode_u32_le(&self.data[self.restart_offset + i * 4..]) as usize\n    }\n\n    /// Decode the entry header at absolute payload offset `pos`.\n    pub fn entry_at(&self, pos: usize) -> Result<EntryHeader> {\n        EntryHeader::decode(&self.data, pos, self.restart_offset)\n    }\n\n    /// Cursor positioned at the first entry.\n    pub fn first(&self) -> Result<Cursor<'_>> {\n        let mut c = Cursor::new(self, 0);\n        c.next()?;\n        Ok(c)\n    }\n\n    /// Position a cursor at the first entry whose key is `>= target`.\n    /// The returned cursor is invalid iff every key is smaller.\n    pub fn seek(&self, target: &[u8]) -> Result<Cursor<'_>> {\n        // Binary search across restart points: find the last restart whose full\n        // key is strictly less than `target`.\n        let mut lo: i64 = 0;\n        let mut hi: i64 = self.num_restarts as i64 - 1;\n        while lo < hi {\n            let mid = (lo + hi + 1) / 2;\n            let key = self.restart_key(mid as usize)?;\n            if key < target {\n                lo = mid;\n            } else {\n                hi = mid - 1;\n            }\n        }\n\n        let mut cur = Cursor::new(self, self.restart_point(lo as usize));\n        while cur.next()? {\n            if cur.key() >= target {\n                return Ok(cur);\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(cur)\n    }\n\n    /// Full key bytes of restart entry `i` (restart entries store shared=0).\n    fn restart_key(&self, i: usize) -> Result<&[u8]> {\n        let off = self.restart_point(i);\n        let h = self.entry_at(off)?;\n        if h.shared != 0 {\n            return Err(Error::corruption(\n                \"restart entry has non-zero shared length\",\n            ));\n        }\n        Ok(&self.data[h.key_delta_offset..h.key_delta_offset + h.non_shared as usize])\n    }\n}\n\n/// Decoded header/locations of one block entry.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct EntryHeader {\n    pub shared: u32,\n    pub non_shared: u32,\n    pub value_len: u32,\n    pub key_delta_offset: usize,\n    pub value_offset: usize,\n    pub next_offset: usize,\n}\n\nimpl EntryHeader {\n    fn decode(data: &[u8], pos: usize, end: usize) -> Result<EntryHeader> {\n        let (shared, n1) = coding::decode_varint32(data, pos)?;\n        let (non_shared, n2) = coding::decode_varint32(data, pos + n1)?;\n        let (value_len, n3) = coding::decode_varint32(data, pos + n1 + n2)?;\n        let key_delta_offset = pos + n1 + n2 + n3;\n        let value_offset = key_delta_offset\n            .checked_add(non_shared as usize)\n            .ok_or_else(|| Error::corruption(\"entry key length overflow\"))?;\n        let next_offset = value_offset\n            .checked_add(value_len as usize)\n            .ok_or_else(|| Error::corruption(\"entry value length overflow\"))?;\n        if next_offset > end {\n            return Err(Error::corruption(\"entry overruns into restart array\"));\n        }\n        Ok(EntryHeader {\n            shared,\n            non_shared,\n            value_len,\n            key_delta_offset,\n            value_offset,\n            next_offset,\n        })\n    }\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Cursor\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/// Forward cursor over a [`Block`]. The reconstructed key is owned here; values\n/// borrow the block bytes.\npub struct Cursor<'a> {\n    block: &'a Block,\n    /// Offset of the next entry to decode.\n    pos: usize,\n    /// Offset of the current entry.\n    entry_offset: usize,\n    valid: bool,\n    key: Vec<u8>,\n}\n\nimpl<'a> Cursor<'a> {\n    fn new(block: &'a Block, start: usize) -> Cursor<'a> {\n        Cursor {\n            block,\n            pos: start,\n            entry_offset: start,\n            valid: false,\n            key: Vec::new(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Restart a scan at restart point `index` (clears the prefix state).\n    fn restart_at(&mut self, index: usize) {\n        self.key.clear();\n        self.pos = self.block.restart_point(index);\n        self.entry_offset = self.pos;\n        self.valid = false;\n    }\n\n    /// Advance to the next entry; returns `false` at end of block.\n    pub fn next(&mut self) -> Result<bool> {\n        if self.pos >= self.block.restart_offset {\n            self.valid = false;\n            return Ok(false);\n        }\n        self.entry_offset = self.pos;\n        let h = self.block.entry_at(self.pos)?;\n        if h.shared as usize > self.key.len() {\n            return Err(Error::corruption(format!(\n                \"entry at {} shares {} bytes but reconstructed key is {} bytes\",\n                self.pos,\n                h.shared,\n                self.key.len()\n            )));\n        }\n        self.key.truncate(h.shared as usize);\n        self.key.extend_from_slice(\n            &self.block.data\n                [h.key_delta_offset..h.key_delta_offset + h.non_shared as usize],\n        );\n        self.pos = h.next_offset;\n        self.valid = true;\n        Ok(true)\n    }\n\n    pub fn valid(&self) -> bool {\n        self.valid\n    }\n\n    pub fn key(&self) -> &[u8] {\n        &self.key\n    }\n\n    /// Value bytes of the current entry (borrowed from the block).\n    pub fn value(&self) -> Result<&'a [u8]> {\n        let h = self.block.entry_at(self.entry_offset)?;\n        Ok(&self.block.data[h.value_offset..h.value_offset + h.value_len as usize])\n    }\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Deep structural validation (used by Table::validate and corruption tests)\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/// Entry statistics gathered during a full block walk.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct BlockStats {\n    pub entries: usize,\n    pub restarts: usize,\n}\n\n/// Walk every entry of `block`, reconstruct all keys and enforce ordering and\n/// restart discipline. A well-formed non-empty block has `entries >= restarts`.\npub fn validate_entries(block: &Block) -> Result<BlockStats> {\n    let mut cur = Cursor::new(block, 0);\n    let mut prev_key: Option<Vec<u8>> = None;\n    let mut entries = 0usize;\n    let mut restart_index = 0usize;\n\n    // Replay positions, tracking where restart points should land.\n    let mut pos = 0usize;\n    while pos < block.restart_offset() {\n        let h = block.entry_at(pos)?;\n        let is_restart_slot = entries % 1 == 0; // placeholder; real rule below\n        let _ = is_restart_slot;\n\n        // Whether this entry is a restart point depends on its position.\n        let should_be_restart = if restart_index < block.num_restarts() {\n            block.restart_point(restart_index) == pos\n        } else {\n            false\n        };\n        if should_be_restart && h.shared != 0 {\n            return Err(Error::corruption(format!(\n                \"entry at {pos} is recorded as a restart point but shares {} bytes\",\n                h.shared\n            )));\n        }\n        if should_be_restart {\n            restart_index += 1;\n        } else if h.shared == 0 {\n            // A non-restart entry may still legitimately share 0 bytes (e.g.\n            // short keys with no common prefix); that is allowed.\n        }\n\n        // Reconstruct via cursor machinery by advancing it.\n        let advanced = cur.next()?;\n        debug_assert!(advanced);\n        if let Some(prev) = &prev_key {\n            if prev.as_slice() >= cur.key() {\n                return Err(Error::corruption(format!(\n                    \"block keys not strictly increasing at entry {entries}\"\n                )));\n            }\n        }\n        prev_key = Some(cur.key().to_vec());\n        entries += 1;\n        pos = h.next_offset;\n    }\n\n    if restart_index != block.num_restarts() {\n        return Err(Error::corruption(format!(\n            \"restart points consumed ({restart_index}) != recorded ({})\",\n            block.num_restarts()\n        )));\n    }\n    if entries < block.num_restarts() {\n        return Err(Error::corruption(\n            \"fewer entries than restart points\",\n        ));\n    }\n    Ok(BlockStats {\n        entries,\n        restarts: block.num_restarts(),\n    })\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use b\"\"),\n                (b\"a3\", b\"\"),\n                (b\"a4\", b\"\"),\n            ],\n        );\n        for target in [b\"a0\".as_ref(), b\"a2\", b\"a3\", b\"a4\"] {\n            let cur = block.seek(target).unwrap();\n            assert!(cur.valid(), \"seek {target:?} invalid\");\n            assert_eq!(cur.key(), target);\n        }\n        let cur = block.seek(b\"a5\").unwrap();\n        assert!(!cur.valid());\n        let cur = block.seek(b\"\").unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(cur.key(), b\"a0\");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn empty_key_is_legal() {\n        let block = assert_eq!(cur.value().unwrap(), b\"v0\");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn common_prefix_compresses() {\n        let mut b = BlockBuilder::new(16).unwrap();\n        b.add(b\"aaaaaaaaaa01\", b\"v\");\n        b.add(b\"aaaaaaaaaa02\", b\"v\");\n        let raw = b.finish();\n        // Keys are 12 bytes each but only 3 suffix bytes should repeat.\n        assert!(raw.len() < 12 + 12 + 16);\n        let block = Block::parse(raw.to_vec()).unwrap();\n        let stats = validate_entries(&block).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(stats.entries, 2);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn Error::Corruption(_)));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn rejects_ordering_violation() {\n        // Hand-build two entries out of order (builder normally prevents it).\n        let mut b = BlockBuilder::new(16).unwrap();\n        b.add(b\"b\", b\"\");\n        b.add(b\"a\", b\"\");\n        let raw = b.finish().to_vec();\n        let block = Block::parse(raw).unwrap();\n {"parentUuid":"e1d01f2b-126e-4da8-bb65-9447e2c1b7f8","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"id":"call_w9a68lp1n913j99wla228ykg","input":{"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp8/b/src/table.rs","content":"//! The sorted table: write path (`TableBuilder`), read path (`Table`),\n//! two-level sparse index lookup, range scans and whole-file validation.\n//!\n//! ## Synchronization boundaries\n//!\n//! Data blocks are appended as they fill, but bytes on disk are not a\n//! committed table until [`TableBuilder::finish`] returns: it writes the\n//! metaindex, index and footer, then issues exactly one `sync_all`. The\n//! file-based helper [`build_table_sorted`] additionally writes to a temp\n//! name, renames over the final name and syncs the parent directory, so a\n//! table file appears atomically and a failed build leaves no final file.\n\nuse std::fs::{self, File};\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\n\nuse crate::block::{self, Block, BlockBuilder, Cursor};\nuse crate::coding;\nuse crate::error::{Error, Result};\nuse crate::format::{\n    self, BlockHandle, Footer, BLOCK_TRAILER_LEN, BLOCK_TYPE_DATA, FOOTER_LEN,\n    MAX_BLOCK_SIZE,\n};\nuse crate::io::{\n    append_all, read_fill, PosixReader, PosixWriter, RandomAccessFile, WritableFile,\n};\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Options\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/// Builder options.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct Options {\n    /// Flush a data block once its estimated encoded size reaches this many\n    /// bytes. (A single larger-than-target entry still gets its own block.)\n    pub block_size: usize,\n    /// Entries between restart points inside a data block.\n    pub restart_interval: u32,\n}\n\nimpl Default for Options {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Options {\n            block_size: 4096,\n            restart_interval: 16,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Options {\n    pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        if self.block_size < 32 {\n            return Err(Error::invalid_argument(\"block_size must be >= 32\"));\n        }\n        if self.block_size > MAX_BLOCK_SIZE {\n            return Err(Error::invalid_argument(\"block_size exceeds maximum\"));\n        }\n        if self.restart_interval == 0 {\n            return Err(Error::invalid_argument(\"restart_interval must be >= 1\"));\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n/// Summary returned by a successful build.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct BuildStats {\n    pub bytes: u64,\n    pub entries: u64,\n    pub data_blocks: u64,\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Write path\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/// Builds one table over a generic [`WritableFile`].\npub struct TableBuilder<W: WritableFile> {\n    writer: W,\n    options: Options,\n    data: BlockBuilder,\n    index: BlockBuilder,\n    last_key: Vec<u8>,\n    offset: u64,\n    num_entries: u64,\n    num_data_blocks: u64,\n    pending_index_entry: bool,\n    pending_handle: Option<BlockHandle>,\n    finished: bool,\n}\n\nimpl<W: WritableFile> TableBuilder<W> {\n    pub fn new(writer: W, options: Options) -> Result<TableBuilder<W>> {\n        options.validate()?;\n        Ok(TableBuilder {\n            writer,\n            data: BlockBuilder::new(options.restart_interval)?,\n            index: BlockBuilder::new(1)?,\n            last_key: Vec::new(),\n            offset: 0,\n            num_entries: 0,\n            num_data_blocks: 0,\n            pending_index_entry: false,\n            pending_handle: None,\n            finished: false,\n            options,\n        })\n    }\n\n    pub fn entries(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.num_entries\n    }\n\n    /// Append a key/value pair. Keys MUST be strictly increasing.\n    pub fn add(&mut self, key: &[u8], value: &[u8]) -> Result<()> {\n        if self.finished {\n            return Err(Error::invalid_argument(\"builder already finished\"));\n        }\n        if self.num_entries > 0 && key <= self.last_key.as_slice() {\n            return Err(Error::invalid_argument(format!(\n                \"keys must be strictly increasing: new key {} <= last key {}\",\n                coding::to_hex(key),\n                coding::to_hex(&self.last_key)\n            )));\n        }\n\n        if self.pending_index_entry {\n            // Emit an index separator for the block flushed earlier.\n            let mut separator = self.last_key.clone();\n            find_shortest_separator(&mut separator, key);\n            let handle = self\n                .pending_handle\n                .take()\n                .expect(\"pending handle must exist\");\n            self.index.add(&separator, &encode_handle(handle));\n            self.pending_index_entry = false;\n        }\n\n        self.data.add(key, value);\n        self.last_key.clear();\n        self.last_key.extend_from_slice(key);\n        self.num_entries += 1;\n\n        if self.data.estimated_size() >= self.options.block_size {\n            self.flush_data_block()?;\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn flush_data_block(&mut self) -> Result<()> {\n        if self.data.is_empty() {\n            self.pending_index_entry = false;\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n        let payload = self.data.finish().to_vec();\n        let handle = append_block(&mut self.writer, self.offset, &payload)?;\n        self.offset = handle.end_exclusive()?;\n        self.data.reset();\n        self.num_data_blocks += 1;\n        self.pending_index_entry = true;\n        self.pending_handle = Some(handle);\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Flush trailing data, write metaindex/index/footer and sync. Consumes the\n    /// builder; the writer itself is dropped afterwards.\n    pub fn finish(mut self) -> Result<BuildStats> {\n        self.flush_data_block()?;\n\n        if self.pending_index_entry {\n            let mut successor = self.last_key.clone();\n            find_short_successor(&mut successor);\n            let handle = self\n                .pending_handle\n                .take()\n                .expect(\"pending handle must exist\");\n            self.index.add(&successor, &encode_handle(handle));\n            self.pending_index_entry = false;\n        }\n\n        // Empty metaindex block (no optional sections in this version).\n        let mut meta = BlockBuilder::new(1)?;\n        let meta_payload = meta.finish().to_vec();\n        let meta_handle = append_block(&mut self.writer, self.offset, &meta_payload)?;\n        self.offset = meta_handle.end_exclusive()?;\n\n        let index_payload = self.index.finish().to_vec();\n        let index_handle = append_block(&mut self.writer, self.offset, &index_payload)?;\n        self.offset = index_handle.end_exclusive()?;\n\n        let mut footer_bytes = Vec::with_capacity(FOOTER_LEN);\n        Footer::new(meta_handle, index_handle).encode_to(&mut footer_bytes)?;\n        append_all(&mut self.writer, &footer_bytes)?;\n        self.offset += footer_bytes.len() as u64;\n\n        // The single durability boundary for the whole table.\n        self.writer.sync()?;\n        self.finished = true;\n\n        Ok(BuildStats {\n            bytes: self.offset,\n            entries: self.num_entries,\n            data_blocks: self.num_data_blocks,\n        })\n    }\n}\n\nfn append_block<W: WritableFile + ?Sized>(\n    w: &mut W,\n    offset: u64,\n    payload: &[u8],\n) -> Result<BlockHandle> {\n    if payload.len() > MAX_BLOCK_SIZE {\n        return Err(Error::invalid_argument(\"block payload exceeds maximum\"));\n    }\n    let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(payload.len() + BLOCK_TRAILER_LEN);\n    let probe = format::write_block(&mut buf, BLOCK_TYPE_DATA, payload);\n    debug_assert_eq!(probe.offset, 0);\n    append_all(w, &buf)?;\n    Ok(BlockHandle::new(offset, payload.len() as u64))\n}\n\nfn encode_handle(h: BlockHandle) -> Vec<u8> {\n    let mut v = Vec::new();\n    h.encode_to(&mut v);\n    v\n}\n\nfn decode_handle_value(value: &[u8]) -> Result<BlockHandle> {\n    let (handle, n) = BlockHandle::decode(value)?;\n    if n != value.len() {\n        return Err(Error::corruption(\"index value has trailing bytes\"));\n    }\n    Ok(handle)\n}\n\n/// Mutate `start` into a short key such that `start <= result < limit`\n/// (LevelDB's `FindShortestSeparator`).\nfn find_shortest_separator(start: &mut Vec<u8>, limit: &[u8]) {\n    let min_len = start.len().min(limit.len());\n    let mut diff = 0;\n    while diff < min_len && start[diff] == limit[diff] {\n        diff += 1;\n    }\n    if diff >= min_len {\n        // One is a prefix of the other: cannot shorten.\n        return;\n    }\n    let diff_byte = start[diff];\n    if diff_byte < 0xff && diff_byte + 1 < limit[diff] {\n        start[diff] += 1;\n        start.truncate(diff + 1);\n    }\n}\n\n/// Shortest key strictly greater than `key` (used as the final index bound).\nfn find_short_successor(key: &mut Vec<u8>) {\n    for b in key.iter_mut() {\n        if *b != 0xff {\n            *b += 1;\n            let pos = b.as_slice().as_ptr() as usize - key.as_ptr() as usize;\n            key.truncate(pos + 1);\n            return;\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// File-based atomic build\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/// Sort and strictly validate `entries`, then build `dir/name` atomically.\n///\n/// The temp file is removed on any error. `unique_suffix` must make the temp\n/// name unique among concurrent builds in the same directory.\npub fn build_table_sorted(\n    dir: &Path,\n    name: &str,\n    entries: &[(Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>)],\n    options: Options,\n    unique_suffix: u64,\n) -> Result<BuildStats> {\n    validate_table_name(name)?;\n    let mut sorted: Vec<&(Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>)> = entries.iter().collect();\n    sorted.sort_by(|a, b| a.0.cmp(&b.0));\n    for pair in sorted.windows(2) {\n        if pair[0].0 == pair[1].0 {\n            return Err(Error::invalid_argument(format!(\n                \"duplicate key: {}\",\n                coding::to_hex(&pair[0].0)\n            )));\n        }\n    }\n\n    let final_path = dir.join(name);\n    let tmp_name = format!(\".{name}.tmp.{unique_suffix}\");\n    let tmp_path = dir.join(&tmp_name);\n\n    let result = (|| -> Result<BuildStats> {\n        let writer = PosixWriter::create(&tmp_path)?;\n        let mut builder = TableBuilder::new(writer, options)?;\n        for (k, v) in &sorted {\n            builder.add(k, v)?;\n        }\n        let stats = builder.finish()?;\n        fs::rename(&tmp_path, &final_path)?;\n        // Sync the directory entry so the rename itself is durable.\n        sync_directory(dir)?;\n        Ok(stats)\n    })();\n\n    if result.is_err() {\n        let _ = fs::remove_file(&tmp_path);\n    }\n    result\n}\n\npub fn validate_table_name(name: &str) -> Result<()> {\n    if name.is_empty()\n        || name == \".\"\n        || name == \"..\"\n        || name.contains('/')\n        || name.contains('\\\\')\n        || name.contains('\\0')\n    {\n        return Err(Error::invalid_argument(\n            \"table name must be a non-empty path component without /, \\\\ or NUL\",\n        ));\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nfn sync_directory(dir: &Path) -> Result<()> {\n    let f = File::open(dir)?;\n    f.sync_all()?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Read path\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/// An open, read-only table.\npub struct Table<R: RandomAccessFile> {\n    file: R,\n    file_size: u64,\n    footer: Footer,\n    index_block: Block,\n}\n\nimpl Table<PosixReader> {\n    /// Open a table directly from a filesystem path.\n    pub fn open_path(path: &Path) -> Result<Table<PosixReader>> {\n        let size = fs::metadata(path)?.len();\n        Table::open(PosixReader::open(path)?, size)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<R: RandomAccessFile> Table<R> {\n    /// Open a table. Only the footer and the index block are read eagerly\n    /// (fail fast); data blocks are read on demand.\n    pub fn open(file: R, file_size: u64) -> Result<Table<R>> {\n        if file_size < FOOTER_LEN as u64 {\n            return Err(Error::corruption(format!(\n                \"file too small to contain a footer: {file_size} bytes\"\n            )));\n        }\n        let footer = {\n            let mut buf = vec![0u8; FOOTER_LEN];\n            let off = file_size - FOOTER_LEN as u64;\n            let n = read_fill(&file, &mut buf, off)?;\n            if n != FOOTER_LEN {\n                return Err(Error::corruption(\"short footer read\"));\n            }\n            Footer::decode(&buf)?\n        };\n        let index_block = read_block_checked(&file, file_size, footer.index)?;\n        Ok(Table {\n            file,\n            file_size,\n            footer,\n            index_block,\n        })\n    }\n\n    pub fn file_size(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.file_size\n    }\n\n    pub fn data_block_count_from_index(&self) -> Result<usize> {\n        // Index holds exactly one entry per data block.\n        let mut cur = self.index_block.first()?;\n        let mut n = 0;\n        while cur.valid() {\n            n += 1;\n            cur.next()?;\n        }\n        Ok(n)\n    }\n\n    /// Point lookup: `Some(value)` iff `key` exists.\n    pub fn get(&self, key: &[u8]) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>> {\n        let handle = match self.index_handle_for(key)? {\n            Some(h) => h,\n            None => return Ok(None),\n        };\n        let block = self.read_block(handle)?;\n        let cur = block.seek(key)?;\n        if cur.valid() && cur.key() == key {\n            Ok(Some(cur.value()?.to_vec()))\n        } else {\n            Ok(None)\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Open a forward range scan.\n    pub fn scan(&self, options: ScanOptions) -> Result<ScanIter<'_, R>> {\n        ScanIter::new(self, options)\n    }\n\n    fn index_handle_for(&self, key: &[u8]) -> Result<Option<BlockHandle>> {\n        let cur = self.index_block.seek(key)?;\n        if !cur.valid() {\n            return Ok(None);\n        }\n        Ok(Some(decode_handle_value(cur.value()?)?))\n    }\n\n    fn read_block(&self, handle: BlockHandle) -> Result<Block> {\n        read_block_checked(&self.file, self.file_size, handle)\n    }\n\n    /// Read every byte of the file and enforce every format invariant.\n    pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<ValidationReport> {\n        let mut report = ValidationReport {\n            file_size: self.file_size,\n            ..ValidationReport::default()\n        };\n\n        // 1. Footer must sit exactly at end of file and carry the magic.\n        let mut footer_bytes = vec![0u8; FOOTER_LEN];\n        let n = read_fill(\n            &self.file,\n            &mut footer_bytes,\n            self.file_size - FOOTER_LEN as u64,\n        )?;\n        if n != FOOTER_LEN {\n            return Err(Error::corruption(\"short footer read during validate\"));\n        }\n        let footer = Footer::decode(&footer_bytes)?;\n\n        // 2. Handle bounds and the block ordering footer -> data.\n        let index_end = footer\n            .index\n            .end_exclusive()\n            .and_then(|e| check_inside_file(e, self.file_size))?;\n        if index_end != self.file_size - FOOTER_LEN as u64 {\n            return Err(Error::corruption(\n                \"index block is not directly followed by the footer\",\n            ));\n        }\n        let meta_end = footer\n            .metaindex\n            .end_exclusive()\n            .and_then(|e| check_inside_file(e, self.file_size))?;\n        if meta_end != footer.index.offset {\n            return Err(Error::corruption(\n                \"metaindex block is not directly followed by the index block\",\n            ));\n        }\n\n        // 3. Metaindex: structurally valid and empty in this version.\n        let meta_block = read_block_checked(&self.file, self.file_size, footer.metaindex)?;\n        let meta_stats = block::validate_entries(&meta_block)?;\n        if meta_stats.entries != 0 {\n            return Err(Error::corruption(format!(\n                \"metaindex must be empty, found {} entries\",\n                meta_stats.entries\n            )));\n        }\n\n        // 4. Index block: walk entries and check handles are contiguous and\n        //    bounded.\n        let index_block = read_block_checked(&self.file, self.file_size, footer.index)?;\n        let index_stats = block::validate_entries(&index_block)?;\n        let mut expected_offset = 0u64;\n        let mut prev_last_key: Option<Vec<u8>> = None;\n        let mut cur = index_block.first()?;\n        while cur.valid() {\n            let sep = cur.key().to_vec();\n            let handle = decode_handle_value(cur.value()?)?;\n            if handle.offset != expected_offset {\n                return Err(Error::corruption(format!(\n                    \"data block gap/overlap at offset {} (expected {expected_offset})\",\n                    handle.offset\n                )));\n            }\n            let end = handle\n                .end_exclusive()\n                .and_then(|e| check_inside_file(e, self.file_size))?;\n            if end > footer.metaindex.offset {\n                return Err(Error::corruption(\"data block runs past metaindex\"));\n            }\n            expected_offset = end;\n\n            // 5. The referenced data block itself.\n            let data_block = read_block_checked(&self.file, self.file_size, handle)?;\n            let stats = block::validate_entries(&data_block)?;\n            report.total_entries += stats.entries;\n            report.total_restarts += stats.restarts;\n            report.data_blocks.push(BlockReport {\n                offset: handle.offset,\n                payload_size: handle.size,\n                entries: stats.entries,\n                restarts: stats.restarts,\n            });\n\n            // 6. Cross-block ordering and separator correctness.\n            let first = data_block.first()?;\n            if let Some(last) = &prev_last_key {\n                if last.as_slice() >= first.key() {\n                    return Err(Error::corruption(\n                        \"keys do not increase across the data block boundary\",\n                    ));\n                }\n            }\n            // Separator: >= last key of its block and < first key of the next\n            // block (the final successor is checked separately against EOF).\n            let mut last_cur = first;\n            while last_cur.next()? {}\n            let last_key = last_cur.key().to_vec();\n            if sep.as_slice() < last_key.as_slice() {\n                return Err(Error::corruption(\n                    \"index separator is smaller than the last key of its block\",\n                ));\n            }\n            prev_last_key = Some(last_key);\n\n            cur.next()?;\n        }\n        if expected_offset != footer.metaindex.offset {\n            return Err(Error::corruption(\n                \"data blocks do not tightly precede the metaindex block\",\n            ));\n        }\n        if index_stats.entries != report.data_blocks.len() {\n            return Err(Error::corruption(\n                \"index entry count != data block count\",\n            ));\n        }\n\n        // Final index successor must be strictly greater than the last key.\n        if let Some(last) = prev_last_key {\n            let mut last_cur = index_block.first()?;\n            while last_cur.next()? {}\n            if last_cur.valid() && last_cur.key().as_slice() <= last.as_slice() {\n                return Err(Error::corruption(\n                    \"final index successor is not greater than the last data key\",\n                ));\n            }\n        }\n\n        report.ok = true;\n        Ok(report)\n    }\n}\n\nfn check_inside_file(end: u64, file_size: u64) -> Result<u64> {\n    if end > file_size {\n        return Err(Error::corruption(\"block handle reaches past end of file\"));\n    }\n    Ok(end)\n}\n\n/// Read payload + trailer, enforce bounds/type/CRC, then parse the block.\nfn read_block_checked<R: RandomAccessFile + ?Sized>(\n    file: &R,\n    file_size: u64,\n    handle: BlockHandle,\n) -> Result<Block> {\n    if handle.size > MAX_BLOCK_SIZE as u64 {\n        return Err(Error::corruption(format!(\n            \"block size {} exceeds maximum\",\n            handle.size\n        )));\n    }\n    let end = handle\n        .offset\n        .checked_add(handle.size)\n        .and_then(|v| v.checked_add(BLOCK_TRAILER_LEN as u64))\n        .ok_or_else(|| Error::corruption(\"block handle overflow\"))?;\n    if end > file_size {\n        return Err(Error::corruption(format!(\n            \"block at {}+{} reaches past end of file ({file_size})\",\n            handle.offset, handle.size\n        )));\n    }\n\n    let mut payload = vec![0u8; handle.size as usize];\n    let n = read_fill(file, &mut payload, handle.offset)?;\n    if n as u64 != handle.size {\n        return Err(Error::corruption(\"short block payload read\"));\n    }\n    let mut trailer = [0u8; BLOCK_TRAILER_LEN];\n    let n = read_fill(file, &mut trailer, handle.offset + handle.size)?;\n    if n != BLOCK_TRAILER_LEN {\n        return Err(Error::corruption(\"short block trailer read\"));\n    }\n\n    let block_type = trailer[0];\n    if block_type != BLOCK_TYPE_DATA {\n        return Err(Error::corruption(format!(\n            \"unsupported block type {block_type} (only raw data blocks exist)\"\n        )));\n    }\n    let stored = coding::decode_u32_le(&trailer[1..]);\n    let mut crc_input = Vec::with_capacity(1 + payload.len());\n    crc_input.push(block_type);\n    crc_input.extend_from_slice(&payload);\n    let computed = coding::mask_crc(coding::crc32c(&crc_input));\n    if stored != computed {\n        return Err(Error::corruption(format!(\n            \"block checksum mismatch at offset {} (stored {stored:#010x}, computed {computed:#010x})\",\n            handle.offset\n        )));\n    }\n    Block::parse(payload)\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Validation report\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct BlockReport {\n    pub offset: u64,\n    pub payload_size: u64,\n    pub entries: usize,\n    pub restarts: usize,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\npub struct ValidationReport {\n    pub ok: bool,\n    pub file_size: u64,\n    pub data_blocks: Vec<BlockReport>,\n    pub total_entries: usize,\n    pub total_restarts: usize,\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Range scans\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/// One side of a range.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub enum Bound {\n    Unbounded,\n    Included(Vec<u8>),\n    Excluded(Vec<u8>),\n}\n\n/// Scan parameters.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct ScanOptions {\n    pub start: Bound,\n    pub end: Bound,\n    pub limit: Option<u64>,\n}\n\nimpl Default for ScanOptions {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        ScanOptions {\n            start: Bound::Unbounded,\n            end: Bound::Unbounded,\n            limit: None,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Bound {\n    fn as_key(&self) -> Option<&[u8]> {\n        match self {\n            Bound::Unbounded => None,\n            Bound::Included(k) | Bound::Excluded(k) => Some(k),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Per-block manual decode state (a self-referential `Cursor` over our own\n/// owned block is impossible, so the iterator tracks positions itself).\nstruct DataState {\n    block: Block,\n    /// Offset of the next entry to decode (ignored while `primed`).\n    pos: usize,\n    /// Offset of the current entry when primed/returned.\n    cur_offset: usize,\n    key: Vec<u8>,\n    primed: bool,\n}\n\n/// Forward iterator over a contiguous key range, hopping data blocks through\n/// the sparse index on demand.\npub struct ScanIter<'a, R: RandomAccessFile> {\n    table: &'a Table<R>,\n    index_block: &'a Block,\n    idx_pos: usize,\n    idx_key: Vec<u8>,\n    data: Option<DataState>,\n    end: Bound,\n    limit: u64,\n    emitted: u64,\n    done: bool,\n}\n\nimpl<'a, R: RandomAccessFile> ScanIter<'a, R> {\n    fn new(table: &'a Table<R>, options: ScanOptions) -> Result<ScanIter<'a, R>> {\n        let limit = options.limit.unwrap_or(u64::MAX);\n        let mut iter = ScanIter {\n            table,\n            index_block: &table.index_block,\n            idx_pos: 0,\n            idx_key: Vec::new(),\n            data: None,\n            end: options.end,\n            limit,\n            emitted: 0,\n            done: limit == 0,\n        };\n\n        if !iter.done {\n            match &options.start {\n                Bound::Unbounded => {\n                    if !iter.advance_index()? {\n                        iter.done = true;\n                    } else {\n                        iter.load_current_block(None)?;\n                    }\n                }\n                Bound::Included(k) => iter.seek_start(k, false)?,\n                Bound::Excluded(k) => iter.seek_start(k, true)?,\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(iter)\n    }\n\n    /// Position at the first data block/entry relevant for `target`.\n    fn seek_start(&mut self, target: &[u8], skip_equal: bool) -> Result<()> {\n        let mut cur = self.index_block.seek(target)?;\n        if !cur.valid() {\n            self.done = true;\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n        self.idx_pos = cur_entry_offset(&cur);\n        self.idx_key = cur.key().to_vec();\n        let handle = decode_handle_value(cur.value()?)?;\n        let block = self.table.read_block(handle)?;\n\n        let mut dcur = block.seek(target)?;\n        if skip_equal && dcur.valid() && dcur.key() == target {\n            dcur.next()?;\n        }\n        self.prime_from(block, &mut dcur)\n    }\n\n    fn prime_from(&mut self, block: Block, cur: &mut Cursor<'_>) -> Result<()> {\n        if !cur.valid() {\n            self.data = None;\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n        let offset = cur_entry_offset(cur);\n        let h = block.entry_at(offset)?;\n        self.data = Some(DataState {\n            block,\n            pos: h.next_offset,\n            cur_offset: offset,\n            key: cur.key().to_vec(),\n            primed: true,\n        });\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Decode the next index entry; prime `idx_pos/idx_key` and load its block.\n    fn advance_index(&mut self) -> Result<bool> {\n        if self.idx_pos >= self.index_block.restart_offset() {\n            return Ok(false);\n        }\n        let h = self.index_block.entry_at(self.idx_pos)?;\n        if h.shared as usize > self.idx_key.len() {\n            return Err(Error::corruption(\"index entry shared length too large\"));\n        }\n        self.idx_key.truncate(h.shared as usize);\n        self.idx_key.extend_from_slice(\n            &self.index_block.payload()\n                [h.key_delta_offset..h.key_delta_offset + h.non_shared as usize],\n        );\n        self.idx_pos = h.next_offset;\n        Ok(true)\n    }\n\n    /// Load the block described by the current index entry. `prime` optionally\n    /// pre-positions inside it (used by the bounded start); otherwise scanning\n    /// begins at the block's first entry.\n    fn load_current_block(&mut self, prime: Option<&mut Cursor<'_>>) -> Result<()> {\n        // Re-decode the value at the current index entry.\n        let prev = self.idx_pos;\n        let entry_pos = locate_prev_entry_offset(self.index_block, prev)?;\n        let h = self.index_block.entry_at(entry_pos)?;\n        let value = &self.index_block.payload()\n            [h.value_offset..h.value_offset + h.value_len as usize];\n        let handle = decode_handle_value(value)?;\n        let block = self.table.read_block(handle)?;\n        match prime {\n            Some(cur) => self.prime_from(block, cur),\n            None => {\n                self.data = Some(DataState {\n                    block,\n                    pos: 0,\n                    cur_offset: 0,\n                    key: Vec::new(),\n                    primed: false,\n                });\n                Ok(())\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Return the next in-range `(key, value)` pair.\n    pub fn next(&mut self) -> Result<Option<(Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>)>> {\n        loop {\n            if self.done || self.emitted >= self.limit {\n                return Ok(None);\n            }\n\n            if self.data.is_none() {\n                if !self.advance_index()? {\n                    self.done = true;\n                    return Ok(None);\n                }\n                self.load_current_block(None)?;\n            }\n\n            let ds = self.data.as_mut().expect(\"data state just loaded\");\n            let (entry_offset, key) = if ds.primed {\n                ds.primed = false;\n                (ds.cur_offset, ds.key.clone())\n            } else {\n                if ds.pos >= ds.block.restart_offset() {\n                    self.data = None;\n                    continue;\n                }\n                let offset = ds.pos;\n                let h = ds.block.entry_at(offset)?;\n                if h.shared as usize > ds.key.len() {\n                    return Err(Error::corruption(\n                        \"data entry shared length exceeds reconstructed key\",\n                    ));\n                }\n                ds.key.truncate(h.shared as usize);\n                ds.key.extend_from_slice(\n                    &ds.block.payload()\n                        [h.key_delta_offset..h.key_delta_offset + h.non_shared as usize],\n                );\n                ds.cur_offset = offset;\n                ds.pos = h.next_offset;\n                (offset, ds.key.clone())\n            };\n\n            // Apply the end bound.\n            match &self.end {\n                Bound::Unbounded => {}\n                Bound::Included(k) if key.as_slice() <= k.as_slice() => {}\n                Bound::Excluded(k) if key.as_slice() < k.as_slice() => {}\n                Bound::Included(_) | Bound::Excluded(_) => {\n                    self.done = true;\n                    return Ok(None);\n                }\n            }\n\n            let ds = self.data.as_ref().expect(\"data state present\");\n            let h = ds.block.entry_at(entry_offset)?;\n            let value = ds.block.payload()\n                [h.value_offset..h.value_offset + h.value_len as usize]\n                .to_vec();\n\n            self.emitted += 1;\n            return Ok(Some((key, value)));\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Public
