fails.\n            fail_append_at: Some(0),\n            ..WriteFaults::default()\n        },\n    );\n    let mut builder = TableBuilder::new(writer, Options::default()).unwrap();\n    let mut failed = false;\n    for (k, v) in &pairs {\n        if builder.add(k, v).is_err() {\n            failed = true;\n            break;\n        }\n    }\n    if !failed {\n        let err = builder.finish().unwrap_err();\n        assert!(matches!(err, Error::Io(_)), \"got {err}\");\n    }\n    // Whatever partial bytes exist must not parse as a table.\n    let open = Table::open(MemReader::new(store.clone()), store.len() as u64);\n    assert!(matches!(open, Err(Error::Io(_)) | Err(Error::Corruption(_))));\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn injected_late_append_failure_during_finish() {\n    let pairs = sample_pairs();\n    let store = MemStore::new();\n    // Count appends: with tiny blocks there are several data appends; make the\n    // index-block append (one of the last) fail instead.\n    let writer = CountingWriter::new(MemWriter::new(store.clone()));\n    let mut builder = TableBuilder::new(\n        writer,\n        Options {\n            block_size: 64,\n            restart_interval: 4,\n        },\n    )\n    .unwrap();\n    for (k, v) in &pairs {\n        builder.add(k, v).unwrap();\n    }\n    // Drain to count expected appends is awkward through the consumed builder;\n    // instead rebuild with a fault at a high call index guaranteed to land on\n    // one of the finish-time appends for this data set.\n    drop(builder);\n\n    let store2 = MemStore::new();\n    let writer = FaultyWriter::new(\n        MemWriter::new(store2.clone()),\n        WriteFaults {\n            fail_append_at: Some(40),\n            ..WriteFaults::default()\n        },\n    );\n    let mut builder = TableBuilder::new(\n        writer,\n        Options {\n            block_size: 64,\n            restart_interval: 4,\n        },\n    )\n    .unwrap();\n    for (k, v) in &pairs {\n        builder.add(k, v).unwrap();\n    }\n    let err = builder.finish().unwrap_err();\n    assert!(matches!(err, Error::Io(_)), \"finish error: {err}\");\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn injected_sync_failure_propagates_from_finish() {\n    let pairs = sample_pairs();\n    let store = MemStore::new();\n    let writer = FaultyWriter::new(\n        MemWriter::new(store),\n        WriteFaults {\n            fail_sync_at: Some(0),\n            ..WriteFaults::default()\n        },\n    );\n    let mut builder = TableBuilder::new(writer, error: {err}\");\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn short_writes_are_retried_and_file_is_byte_identical() {\n    let pairs = sample_pairs();\n    let (good_store, size) = build_mem(&pairs, tiny_options()).unwrap();\n\n    let faulty_store = MemStore::new();\n    let writer = FaultyWriter::new(\n        MemWriter::new(faulty_store.clone()),\n        WriteFaults {\n            // Every append only accepts 1..=7 bytes, repeatedly.\n            short_write_at: Some((u64::MAX, 0)), // never triggers by exact index\n            ..WriteFaults::default()\n        },\n    );\n    drop(writer);\n\n    // Instead exercise repeated short writes across *all* appends with a\n    // dedicated writer wrapper below.\n    let faulty_store2 = MemStore::new();\n    let writer = AlwaysShort {\n        inner: MemWriter::new(faulty_store2.clone()),\n        max: 3,\n    };\n    let mut builder = TableBuilder::new(writer, tiny_options()).unwrap();\n    for (k, v) in &pairs {\n        builder.add(k, v).unwrap();\n    }\n    let stats = builder.finish().unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(stats.bytes, size);\n    assert_eq!(faulty_store2.snapshot(), good_store.snapshot());\n\n    // And the resulting table reads correctly.\n    let table = Table::open(MemReader::new(faulty_store2.clone()), size).unwrap();\n    table.validate().unwrap();\n    let all = collect_scan(&table, = build_mem(&pairs, tiny_options()).unwrap();\n    let reader = FaultyReader::new(\n        MemReader::new(store),\n        ReadFaults {\n            max_bytes_per_read: Some(7),\n            ..ReadFaults::default()\n        },\n    );\n    let table = Table::open(reader, size).unwrap();\n    table.validate().unwrap();\n    for (k, v) in pairs.iter().step_by(7) {\n        assert_eq!(table.get(k).unwrap().as_ref(), Some(v));\n    }\n    let all = collect_scan(&table, ScanOptions::default()).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(all.len(), pairs.len());\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn injected_read_error_during_footer_open_surfaces_as_io() {\n    let pairs = sample_pairs();\n    let (store, size) = build_mem(&pairs, tiny_options()).unwrap();\n    let reader = FaultyReader::new(\n        MemReader::new(store),\n        ReadFaults {\n            // The first read fetches the footer; fail it.\n            fail_read_at_call: Some(0),\n            ..ReadFaults::default()\n        },\n    );\n    let err = Table::open(reader, size).unwrap_err();\n    assert!(matches!(err, Error::Io(_)), \"got {err}\");\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn injected_read_error_during_get_surfaces_as_io() {\n    let psst::io::WritableFile for AlwaysShort<W> {\n    fn append(&mut self, data: &[u8]) -> psst::Result<usize> {\n        let n = self.max.min(data.len()).max(1);\n        self.inner.append(&data[..n])\n    }\n    fn sync(&mut self) -> psst::Result<()> {\n        self.inner.sync()\n    }\n}\n\nstruct CountingWriter<W> {\n    inner: W,\n}\nimpl<W> CountingWriter<W> {\n    fn new(inner: W) -> Self {\n        CountingWriter { inner }\n    }\n}\nimpl<W: psst::io::WritableFile> psst::io::WritableFile for CountingWriter<W> {\n    fn append(&mut self, data: &[u8]) -> psst::Result<usize> {\n        self.inner.append(data)\n    }\n    fn sync(&mut self) -> psst::Result<()> {\n        self.inner.sync()\n    }\n}\n\nstruct BadWriter;\nimpl psst::io::WritableFile for BadWriter {\n    fn append(&mut self, _data: &[u8]) -> psst::Result<usize> {\n        Ok(0) // append_all must treat zero progress as an error\n    }\n    fn sync(&mut self) -> psst::Result<()> {\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\nstruct OverReader;\nimpl psst::io::RandomAccessFile for OverReader {\n    fn read_at(&self, buf: &mut [u8], _offset: u64) -> psst::Result<usize> {\n        Ok(buf.len() + 1) // impossible count\n Binary codecs used by the disk format.\n//!\n//! All multi-byte fixed-width integers are little-endian. Lengths inside blocks\n//! are 32-bit varints (as in LevelDB's block format); block handles and the\n//! footer use 64-bit varints.\n//!\n//! Checksums are CRC32C (Castagnoli), stored **masked** so that a block which\n//! itself happens to contain an unmasked CRC cannot be confused with its own\n//! checksum; the mask follows LevelDB's `Mask(...)`/`Unmask(...)`.\n\nuse crate::error::{Error, Result};\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Fixed-width little-endian helpers\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\npub fn put_u16_le(out: &mut Vec<u8>, v: u16) {\n    out.extend_from_slice(&v.to_le_bytes());\n}\n\npub fn put_u32_le(out: &mut Vec<u8>, v: u32) {\n    out.extend_from_slice(&v.to_le_bytes());\n}\n\npub fn put_u64_le(out: &mut Vec<u8>, v: u64) {\n    out.extend_from_slice(&v.to_le_bytes());\n}\n\n/// Read a little-endian u32 from `buf` (assumed long enough by the caller).\npub fn decode_u32_le(buf: &[u8]) -> u32 {\n    u32::from_le_bytes([buf[0], buf[1], buf[2], buf[3]])\n}\n\n/// Read a little-endian u64 from `buf` (assumed long enough by the caller).\npub fn decode_u64_le(buf: &[u8]) -> u64 {\n    u64::from_le_bytes([\n        buf[0], buf[1], buf[2], buf[3], buf[4], buf[5], buf[6], buf[7],\n    ])\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Varints\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/// Append `value` as a 64-bit varint (at most 10 bytes).\npub fn put_varint64(out: &mut Vec<u8>, mut value: u64) {\n    loop {\n        let mut b = (value & 0x7f) as u8;\n        value >>= 7;\n        if value != 0 {\n            b |= 0x80;\n        }\n        out.push(b);\n        if value == 0 {\n            break;\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Append `value` as a 32-bit varint (at most 5 bytes).\npub fn put_varint32(out: &mut Vec<u8>, value: u32) {\n    put_varint64(out, value as u64);\n}\n\n/// Decode a 64-bit varint starting at `buf[offset]`.\n///\n/// On success returns `(value, bytes_consumed)`. Overlong encodings (extra\n/// all-zero groups) and encodings exceeding 64 bits are rejected.\npub fn decode_varint64(buf: &[u8], offset: usize) -> Result<(u64, usize)> {\n    let mut result: u64 = 0;\n    let mut shift = 0u32;\n    let mut pos = offset;\n    loop {\n        if pos >= buf.len() {\n            return Err(Error::corruption(\"truncated varint\"));\n        }\n        if shift >= 64 {\n            return Err(Error::corruption(\"varint too long\"));\n        }\n        let b = buf[pos];\n        pos += 1;\n        let chunk = (b & 0x7f) as u64;\n        if shift == 63 && chunk > 1 {\n            return Err(Error::corruption(\"varint overflows 64 bits\"));\n        }\n        result |= chunk << shift;\n        if b & 0x80 == 0 {\n            // Reject overlong encoding: a final continuation group must carry\n            // at least one payload bit.\n            if pos - offset > 1 && chunk == 0 {\n                return Err(Error::corruption(\"overlong varint\"));\n            }\n            return Ok((result, pos - offset));\n        }\n        shift += 7;\n    }\n}\n\n/// Decode a 32-bit varint; rejects encodings whose value overflows u32.\npub fn decode_varint32(buf: &[u8], offset: usize) -> Result<(u32, usize)> {\n    let (v, n) = decode_varint64(buf, offset)?;\n    if v > u32::MAX as u64 {\n        return Err(Error::corruption(\"varint overflows 32 bits\"));\n    }\n    Ok((v as u32, n))\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// CRC32C (Castagnoli), software table implementation\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nconst CRC32C_POLY: u32 = 0x82f63b78; // reversed Castagnoli polynomial\n\nstruct CrcTable {\n    entries: [u32; 256],\n}\n\nimpl CrcTable {\n    fn build() -> CrcTable {\n        let mut entries = [0u32; 256];\n        for i in 0..256u32 {\n            let mut crc = i;\n            for _ in 0..8 {\n                crc = (crc >> 1) ^ (CRC32C_POLY & ((crc & 1).wrapping_neg()));\n            }\n            entries[i as usize] = crc;\n        }\n        CrcTable { entries }\n    }\n}\n\nfn crc_table() -> &'static [u32; 256] {\n    use std::sync::OnceLock;\n    static TABLE: OnceLock<CrcTable> = OnceLock::new();\n    &TABLE.get_or_init(CrcTable::build).entries\n}\n\n/// Compute CRC32C over `data` (initial value 0, no final XOR, matching the\n/// LevelDB `crc32c::Value` convention).\npub fn crc32c(data: &[u8]) -> u32 {\n    crc32c_extend(0, data)\n}\n\n/// Continue a CRC32C computation with `data`.\npub fn crc32c_extend(initial: u32, data: &[u8]) -> u32 {\n    let table = crc_table();\n    let mut crc = initial;\n    for &b in data {\n        crc = table[((crc ^ b as u32) & 0xff) as usize] ^ (crc >> 8);\n    }\n    crc\n}\n\n/// Deliberate non-linear mask so a raw CRC embedded in payload bytes cannot be\n/// mistaken for the stored checksum.\npub const CRC_MASK_DELTA: u32 = 0xa282_ead8;\n\npub fn mask_crc(crc: u32) -> u32 {\n    ((crc >> 15) | (crc << 17)).wrapping_add(CRC_MASK_DELTA)\n}\n\npub fn unmask_crc(masked: u32) -> u32 {\n    let rot = masked.wrapping_sub(CRC_MASK_DELTA);\n    (rot >> 17) | (rot << 15)\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Hex helpers (HTTP layer exchanges binary keys/values as hex strings)\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\npub fn to_hex(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {\n    const HEX: &[u8; 16] = b\"0123456789abcdef\";\n    let mut out = String::with_capacity(bytes.len() * 2);\n    for b in bytes {\n        out.push(HEX[(b >> 4) as usize] as char);\n        out.push(HEX[(b & 0x0f) as usize] as char);\n    }\n    out\n}\n\npub fn from_hex(s: &str) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {\n    if s.len() % 2 != 0 {\n        return Err(Error::invalid_argument(\"hex string has odd length\"));\n    }\n    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(s.len() / 2);\n    let bytes = s.as_bytes();\n    let mut i = 0;\n    while i < bytes.len() {\n        let hi = hex_digit(bytes[i])?;\n        let lo = hex_digit(bytes[i + 1])?;\n        out.push((hi << 4) | lo);\n        i += 2;\n    }\n    Ok(out)\n}\n\nfn hex_digit(b: u8) -> Result<u8> {\n    match b {\n        b'0'..=b'9' => Ok(b - b'0'),\n        b'a'..=b'f' => Ok(b - b'a' + 10),\n        b'A'..=b'F' => Ok(b - b'A' + 10),\n        _ => Err(Error::invalid_argument(format!(\n            \"invalid hex digit: {}\",\n            b as char\n        ))),\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn varint_roundtrip() {\n        for v in [\n            0u64,\n            1,\n            127,\n            128,\n            16383,\n            16384,\n            u32::MAX as u64,\n            u64::MAX,\n            1u64 << 63,\n        ] {\n            let mut buf = Vec::new();\n            put_varint64(&mut buf, v);\n            let (got, n) = decode_varint64(&buf, 0).unwrap();\n            assert_eq!(got, v);\n            assert_eq!(n, buf.len());\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn varint_rejects_truncated_and_overlong() {\n        assert!(decode_varint64(&[0x80], 0).is_err());\n        // 0 encoded with an extra zero continuation group.\n        assert!(decode_varint64(&[0x80, 0x00], 0).is_err());\n        // 10 groups carrying 65 bits.\n        assert!(decode_varint64(\n            &[0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x02],\n            0\n        )\n        .is_err());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn crc32c_known_vectors() {\n        // RFC 3720 / crc32c standard check values (un-masked).\n        assert_eq!(crc32c(b\"\"), 0x0000_0000);\n        assert_eq!(crc32c(b\"123456789\"), 0xe306_9283);\n        // Extending must equal computing over the concatenation.\n        let a = crc32c(b\"hello \");\n        assert_eq!(crc32c_extend(a, b\"world\"), crc32c(b\"hello world\"));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn crc_mask_roundtrip() {\n        for c in [0u32, 1, 0xdead_beef, u32::MAX] {\n            assert_eq!(unmask_crc(mask_crc(c)), c);\n        }\n        // The mask changes the value in the common case.\n        assert_ne!(mask_crc(0xdead_beef), 0xdead_beef);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn hex_roundtrip() {\n        for bytes in [vec![], vec![0x00], vec![0xff, 0x10, 0xab]] {\n            assert_eq!(from_hex(&to_hex(&bytes)).unwrap(), bytes);\n        }\n        assert!(from_hex(\"zz\").is_err());\n Strict format validation: every corruption class must be reported as\n//! `Error::Corruption`, never silently accepted.\n//!\n//! The headline case is a **corrupted restart offset**: a payload mutation alone\n//! would be caught by the block CRC first, so for that case the test recomputes\n//! the (masked) checksum after tampering, forcing the reader past the CRC layer\n//! into structural validation where the restart array is checked.\n\nmod common;\n\nuse common::*;\nuse psst::block::Block;\nuse psst::coding::{self, mask_crc, crc32c};\nuse psst::error::Error;\nuse psst::format::{\n    write_block as encode_block, BlockHandle, Footer, BLOCK_TRAILER_LEN,\n    BLOCK_TYPE_DATA, FOOTER_LEN,\n};\nuse psst::io::MemStore;\nuse psst::table::{Options, ScanOptions};\n\nfn sample_bytes() -> Vec<u8> {\n    let pairs: Vec<(Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>)> = (0..200u32)\n        .map(|i| (format!(\"k/{i:04}\").into_bytes(), format!(\"v{i}\").into_bytes()))\n        .collect();\n    let (store, _) = build_mem(\n        &pairs,\n        Options {\n            block_size: 90,\n            restart_interval: 4,\n        },\n    )\n    .unwrap();\n    store.snapshot()\n}\n\nfn first_data_handle(bytes: &[u8]) -> BlockHandle {\n    let footer = Footer::decode(&bytes[bytes.len() - FOOTER_LEN..]).unwrap();\n    let payload =\n        &bytes[footer.index.offset as usize..footer.index.offset as usize + footer.index.size as usize];\n    let idx = Block::parse(payload.to_vec()).unwrap();\n    let cur = idx.first().unwrap();\n    BlockHandle::decode(cur.value().unwrap()).unwrap().0\n}\n\n/// Recompute the trailer checksum for a block after payload tampering.\nfn repair_checksum(bytes: &mut [u8], handle: BlockHandle) {\n    let start = handle.offset as usize;\n    let size = handle.size as usize;\n    let mut crc_input = Vec::with_capacity(1 + size);\n    crc_input.push(BLOCK_TYPE_DATA);\n    crc_input.extend_from_slice(&bytes[start..start + size]);\n    let crc = mask_crc(crc32c(&crc_input)).to_le_bytes();\n    let trailer = start + size;\n    bytes[trailer] = BLOCK_TYPE_DATA;\n    bytes[trailer + 1..trailer + 5].copy_from_slice(&crc);\n}\n\nfn assert_corruption(store: &MemStore, label: &str, when: When) {\n    let size = store.len() as u64;\n    // Opening itself validates the footer and reads the index block.\n    let open = psst::table::Table::open(psst::io::MemReader::new(store.clone()), size);\n    let result = match (open, when) {\n        (Ok(t), When::Open) => panic!(\"{label}: expected corruption at open, opened fine\"),\n        (Ok(t), When::Get) => t\n            .get(b\"k/00050\")\n            .map(|_| ())\n            .and_then(|_| t.validate().map(|_| ())),\n        (Ok(t), When::Validate) => t.validate().map(|_| ()),\n        (Ok(t), When::Scan) => t\n            .scan(ScanOptions::default())\n            .and_then(|mut it| {\n                while let Some(_) = it.next()? {}\n                Ok(())\n            }),\n        (Err(e), When::Open) => Err(e),\n        (Err(e), _) => Err(e),\n    };\n    match result {\n        Err(Error::Corruption(msg)) => {\n            eprintln!(\"{label}: correctly rejected -> {msg}\");\n        }\n        Err(other) => panic!(\"{label}: expected corruption, got {other}\"),\n        Ok(()) => panic!(\"{label}: corruption went undetected\"),\n    }\n}\n\n#[derive(Clone, Copy)]\nenum When {\n    Open,\n    Get,\n    Validate,\n    Scan,\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn bad_footer_magic_rejected() {\n    let mut bytes = sample_bytes();\n    *bytes.last_mut().unwrap() ^= 0xff;\n    let store = MemStore::new();\n    store.overwrite(&bytes);\n    assert_corruption(&store, \"bad footer magic\", When::Open);\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn truncated_file_rejected() {\n    let bytes = sample_bytes();\n    // Cut off half the footer.\n    let cut = bytes.len() - FOOTER_LEN / 2;\n    let store = MemStore::new();\n    store.overwrite(&bytes[..cut]);\n    assert_corruption(&store, \"truncated file\", When::Open);\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn payload_bitflip_caught_by_checksum() {\n    let mut bytes = sample_bytes();\n    let handle = first_data_handle(&bytes);\n    bytes[handle.offset as usize + 3] ^= 0x01;\n    let store = MemStore::new();\n    store.overwrite(&bytes);\n    assert_corruption(&store, \"payload bitflip\", When::Validate);\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn block_type_byte_rejected() {\n    let mut bytes = sample_bytes();\n    let handle = first_data_handle(&bytes);\n    bytes[handle.offset as usize + handle.size as usize] = 99;\n    let store = MemStore::new();\n    store.overwrite(&bytes);\n    assert_corruption(&store, \"bad block type\", When::Validate);\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn corrupted_first_restart_offset_rejected() {\n    let mut bytes = sample_bytes();\n    let handle = first_data_handle(&bytes);\n    let base = handle.offset as usize;\n    let size = handle.size as usize;\n    // restart[0] is the first u32 of the restart array (4-byte count follows).\n    bytes[base + size - 8] = 0x05; // must be zero\n    repair_checksum(&mut bytes, handle);\n    let store = MemStore::new();\n    store.overwrite(&bytes);\n    assert_corruption(&store, \"restart[0] != 0\", When::Validate);\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn corrupted_restart_offset_into_array_rejected() {\n    let mut bytes = sample_bytes();\n    let handle = first_data_handle(&bytes);\n    let base = handle.offset as usize;\n    let size = handle.size as usize;\n    // Point restart[0] directly at the restart array (>= restart_offset).\n    let bad = (size - 8) as u32;\n    bytes[base + size - 8..base + size - 4].copy_from_slice(&bad.to_le_bytes());\n    repair_checksum(&mut bytes, handle);\n    let store = MemStore::new();\n    store.overwrite(&bytes);\n    assert_corruption(&store, \"restart points into array\", When::Validate);\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn corrupted_non_first_restart_offset_rejected() {\n    let mut bytes = sample_bytes();\n    let handle = first_data_handle(&bytes);\n    let base = restart[0]\", When::Validate);\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn corrupted_entry_length_rejected() {\n    let mut bytes = sample_bytes();\n    let handle = first_data_handle(&bytes);\n    let base = handle.offset as    repair_checksum(&mut bytes, handle);\n    let store = MemStore::new();\n    store.overwrite(&bytes);\n    assert_corruption(&store, \"inflated value length\", When::Validate);\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn index_block_bitflip_rejected_at_open() {\n    let bytes = sample_bytes();\n    let footer = Footer::decode(&bytes[bytes.len() - FOOTER_LEN..]).unwrap();\n    let mut bytes = bytes;\n    // Flip a byte b\"zero\".to_vec()),\n        (vec![0x00, 0x00], b\"zeros\".to_vec()),\n        (b\"a\".to_vec(), b\"a\".to_vec()),\n    ];\n    let (store, _) = build_mem(&pairs, tiny_options()).unwrap();\n    let table = open_mem(&store).unwrap();\n    table.validate().unwrap();\n\n    assert_eq!(table.get(&[]).unwrap(), Some(b\"empty\".to_vec()));\n    assert_eq!(table.get(&[0x00]).unwrap(), Some(b\"zero\".to_vec()));\n    assert_eq!(table.get(&[0x00, 0x00]).unwrap(), Some(b\"zeros\".to_vec()));\n    assert_eq!(table.get(b\"missing\").unwrap(), None);\n\n    let all = collect_scan(&table, ScanOptions::default()).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(all, pairs);\n\n    // Scan starting exactly at the empty key returns everything.\n    let from_empty = collect_scan(\n        &table,\n        ScanOptions {\n            start: Bound::Included(vec![]),\n            end: Bound::Unbounded,\n            limit: None,\n        },\n    )\n    .unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(from_empty, pairs);\n\n    // Start boundary strictly greater than empty skips it.\n    let after_empty = collect_scan(\n        &table,\n        ScanOptions {\n            start: Bound::Excluded(vec![]),\n            end: Bound::Unbounded,\n            limit: None,\n        },\n    )\n    .unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(after_empty, pairs[1..].to_vec());\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn long_common_prefix_still_gets_and_scans() {\n    let prefix = b\"prefix-compression-shared-prefix-\".repeat(20); // ~680 bytes\n    let mut pairs = Vec::new();\n    for i in 0..60u32 {\n        let mut k = prefix.clone();\n        k.extend_from_slice(format!(\"{i:06}\").as_bytes());\n        let mut v = vec![i as u8; 1 + (i as usize % 5)];\n        v.extend_from_slice(b\"value\");\n        pairs.push((k, v));\n    }\n    // Also a key that is a strict prefix of others.\n    pairs.insert(0, (b\"p\".to_vec(), b\"single-p\".to_vec()));\n    pairs.sort_by(|a, b| a.0.cmp(&b.0));\n    pairs.dedup_by(|a, b| a.0 == b.0);\n\n    let (store, raw_size) = build_mem(\n        &pairs,\n        Options {\n            // Blocks hold ~16 entries between restart points, so the 680-byte\n            // shared prefix is stored roughly once per block instead of once\n            // per key — that is exactly what prefix compression buys.\n            block_size: 256,\n            restart_interval: 16,\n        },\n    )\n    .unwrap();\n    let table = open_mem(&store).unwrap();\n    let report = table.validate().unwrap();\n    assert!(report.data_blocks.len() >= 3);\n\n    // Prefix compression must actually shrink the file: naive storage would be\n    // at least sum(key.len()) bytes plus overhead.\n    let naive_keys: usize = pairs.iter().map(|(k, _)| k.len()).sum();\n    assert!(\n        (raw_size as usize) < naive_keys,\n        \"file {raw_size} should be smaller than naive key bytes {naive_keys}\"\n    );\n\n    for (k, v) in &pairs {\n        assert_eq!(table.get(k).unwrap().as_ref(), Some(v));\n    }\n    let all = collect_scan(&table, ScanOptions::default()).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(all, pairs);\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn cross_block_scan_with_narrow_bounds() {\n    // Keys distributed over many blocks; ranges deliberately start and end\n    // inside different blocks and exercise every alignment (block boundary,\n    // restart-point boundary, mid-interval entry).\n    let pairs: sits at a block/ restart boundary.\n    let incl = collect_scan(\n        &table,\n        ScanOptions {\n            start: Bound::Included(b\"k/00000\".to_vec()),\n            end: b\"zero\".to_vec()),\n        (vec![0x00, 0x00], b\"zeros\".to_vec()),\n        (b\"a\".to_vec(), b\"a\".to_vec()),\n    ];\n    let (store, _) = build_mem(&pairs, tiny_options()).unwrap();\n    let ScanOptions::default()).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(all, pairs);\n\n    // Scan starting exactly at the empty key returns everything.\n    let from_empty = collect_scan(\n        &table,\n        ScanOptions {\n            start: Bound::Included(vec![]),\n            end: Bound::Unbounded,\n            limit: None,\n        },\n    )\n    .unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(from_empty, pairs);\n\n    // Start boundary strictly greater than empty skips it.\n    let after_empty = collect_scan(\n        &table,\n        ScanOptions {\n            start: Bound::Excluded(vec![]),\n            end: Bound::Unbounded,\n            limit: None,\n        },\n    )\n    .unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(after_empty, pairs[1..].to_vec());\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn long_common_prefix_still_gets_and_scans() {\n    let prefix = b\"prefix-compression-shared-prefix-\".repeat(20); // ~680 bytes\n    let mut pairs = Vec::new();\n    for i in 0..60u32 {\n        let mut k = prefix.clone();\n        k.extend_from_slice(format!(\"{i:06}\").as_bytes());\n        let mut v = vec![i as u8; 1 + (i as usize % 5)];\n        v.extend_from_slice(b\"value\");\n        pairs.push((k, v));\n    }\n    // Also a key that is a strict prefix of others.\n    pairs.insert(0, (b\"p\".to_vec(), b\"single-p\".to_vec()));\n    pairs.sort_by(|a, b| a.0.cmp(&b.0));\n    pairs.dedup_by(|a, b| a.0 == b.0);\n\n    let (store, raw_size) = build_mem(\n        &pairs,\n        Options {\n            // The target must exceed one full ~700-byte restart entry,\n            // otherwise every block holds a single entry with a full key.\n            // At 8 KiB each block holds several entries that share the\n            // 680-byte prefix — that is exactly what prefix compression buys.\n            block_size: 8 * 1024,\n            restart_interval: 16,\n        },\n    )\n    .unwrap();\n    let table = open_mem(&store).unwrap();\n    let report = table.validate().unwrap();\n    assert!(report.data_blocks.len() >= 2);\n\n    // Prefix compression must actually shrink the file: naive storage would be\n    // at least sum(key.len()) bytes plus overhead.\n    let naive_keys: format!(\"k/{i:05}\").into_bytes(),\n                format!(\"v{i}\").into_bytes(),\n            )\n        })\n        .collect();\n    let (store, _) = build_mem(\n        &pairs,\n        Options assert_eq!(mid.first().unwrap().0, b\"k/00100\");\n    assert_eq!(mid.last().unwrap().0, b\"k/00399\");\n\n    // Inclusive end on a key that sits at a block/ restart boundary.\n    let incl =       },\n    )\n    .unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(incl.len(), 5);\n\n    // Start strictly between existing keys.\n    let gap = collect_scan(\n        &table,\n        ScanOptions {\n            start: gap.iter().map(|(k, _)| k.clone()).collect::<Vec<_>>(),\n        vec![b\"k/00124\".to_vec(), b\"k/00125\".to_vec()]\n    );\n\n    // Empty range: start past the end.\n    let none = collect_scan(\n assert!(none.is_empty());\n\n    // Empty range contained within one block gap.\n    let none2 = collect_scan(\n        &table,\n        ScanOptions {\n            start: // Limit applied mid cross-block scan.\n    let lim = collect_scan(\n        &table,\n        ScanOptions {\n            start: Bound::Included(b\"k/00000\".to_vec()),\n            end: A high call index is guaranteed to hit finish-time\n    // appends for this 300-entry data set.\n    let pairs = sample_pairs();\n    let store = MemStore::new();\n    let writer = FaultyWriter::new(\n        MemWriter::new(store),\n        WriteFaults {\n            fail_append_at: Some(40),\n            ..WriteFaults::default()\n        },\n    );\n    let mut builder = TableBuilder::new(\n        writer,\n        Options {\n            block_size: 64,\n            restart_interval: 4,\n        },\n    )\n    .unwrap();\n    for (k, v) in &pairs {\n        builder.add(k, v).unwrap();\n    }\n    let err = builder.finish().unwrap_err();\n    assert!(matches!(err, Error::Io(_)), \"finish error: {err}\");\n}","newString":"#[test]\nfn injected_late_append_failure_aborts_build() {\n    // Tiny blocks produce many append calls; a high call index lands deep in\n    // the build (possibly in finish), and wherever it lands it must surface as\n    // an IO error rather than a corrupt-but-accepted file.\n    let pairs = sample_pairs();\n    let store = MemStore::new();\n    let writer = FaultyWriter::new(\n        MemWriter::new(store.clone()),\n        WriteFaults {\n            fail_append_at: Some(40),\n            ..WriteFaults::default()\n        },\n    );\n    let mut builder = TableBuilder::new(\n        writer,\n        Options {\n            block_size: 64,\n            restart_interval: 4,\n        },\n    )\n    .unwrap();\n\n    let mut failed = false;\n    for (k, v) in &pairs {\n        if builder.add(k, v).is_err() {\n            failed = true;\n            break;\n        }\n    }\n    if !failed {\n        let err = builder.finish().unwrap_err();\n        assert!(matches!(err, Error::Io(_)), \"finish error: {err}\");\n    }\n\n    let open = Table::open(MemReader::new(store.clone()), store.len() as u64);\n    assert!(matches!(open, Err(Error::Io(_)) | Err(Error::Corruption(_))));\n}","originalFile":"//! Injectable I/O layer: injected write/read faults surface as `Error::Io`,\n//! the storage layer retries partial writes and fragmented reads, and the\n//! durability boundary (`sync`) is exercised explicitly.\n\nmod common;\n\nuse common::*;\nuse psst::error::Error;\nuse psst::io::{\n    append_all, read_fill, FaultyReader, FaultyWriter, MemReader, MemStore,\n    MemWriter, ReadFaults, WriteFaults,\n};\nuse psst::table::{collect_scan, Options, ScanOptions, Table, TableBuilder};\n\nfn sample_pairs() -> Vec<(Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>)> {\n    (0..300u32)\n        .map(|i| (format!(\"k/{i:04}\").into_bytes(), format!(\"v{i}\").into_bytes()))\n        .collect()\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn injected_append_failure_aborts_build_and_leaves_no_success() {\n    let pairs = sample_pairs();\n    let store = MemStore::new();\n    let writer = FaultyWriter::new(\n        MemWriter::new(store.clone()),\n        WriteFaults {\n            // The very first data block append fails.\n            fail_append_at: Some(0),\n            ..WriteFaults::default()\n        },\n    );\n    let mut builder = TableBuilder::new(writer, Options::default()).unwrap();\n    let mut failed = false;\n    for (k, v) in &pairs {\n        if builder.add(k, v).is_err() {\n            failed = true;\n            break;\n        }\n    }\n    if !failed {\n        let err = builder.finish().unwrap_err();\n        assert!(matches!(err, Error::Io(_)), \"got {err}\");\n    }\n    // Whatever partial bytes exist must not parse as a table.\n    let open = Table::open(MemReader::new(store.clone()), store.len() as u64);\n    assert!(matches!(open, Err(Error::Io(_)) | Err(Error::Corruption(_))));\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn injected_late_append_failure_during_finish() {\n    // Tiny blocks: appends 0.. are data blocks, and metaindex/index/footer\n    // appends come late. A high call index is guaranteed to hit finish-time\n    // appends for this 300-entry data set.\n    let pairs = sample_pairs();\n    let store = MemStore::new();\n    let writer = FaultyWriter::new(\n        MemWriter::new(store),\n        WriteFaults {\n            fail_append_at: Some(40),\n            ..WriteFaults::default()\n        },\n    );\n    let mut builder = TableBuilder::new(\n        writer,\n        Options {\n            block_size: 64,\n            restart_interval: 4,\n        },\n    )\n    .unwrap();\n    for (k, v) in &pairs {\n        builder.add(k, v).unwrap();\n    }\n    let err = builder.finish().unwrap_err();\n    assert!(matches!(err, Error::Io(_)), \"finish error: {err}\");\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn injected_sync_failure_propagates_from_finish() {\n    let pairs = sample_pairs();\n    let store = MemStore::new();\n    let writer = FaultyWriter::new(\n        MemWriter::new(store),\n        WriteFaults {\n            fail_sync_at: Some(0),\n            ..WriteFaults::default()\n        },\n    );\n    let mut builder = TableBuilder::new(writer, Options::default()).unwrap();\n    for (k, v) in &pairs {\n        builder.add(k, v).unwrap();\n    }\n    let err = builder.finish().unwrap_err();\n    assert!(matches!(err, Error::Io(_)), \"sync error: {err}\");\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn short_writes_are_retried_and_file_is_byte_identical() {\n    let pairs = sample_pairs();\n    let (good_store, size) = build_mem(&pairs, tiny_options()).unwrap();\n\n    // Every append accepts at most 3 bytes; the builder's retry loop must\n    // produce a byte-identical file.\n    let faulty_store = MemStore::new();\n    let writer = AlwaysShort {\n        inner: MemWriter::new(faulty_store.clone()),\n        max: 3,\n    };\n    let mut builder = TableBuilder::new(writer, tiny_options()).unwrap();\n    for (k, v) in &pairs {\n        builder.add(k, v).unwrap();\n    }\n    let stats = builder.finish().unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(stats.bytes, size);\n    assert_eq!(faulty_store.snapshot(), good_store.snapshot());\n\n    // And the resulting table reads correctly.\n    let table = Table::open(MemReader::new(faulty_store.clone()), size).unwrap();\n    table.validate().unwrap();\n    let all = collect_scan(&table, ScanOptions::default()).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(all.len(), pairs.len());\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn fragmented_reads_still_produce_correct_results() {\n    let pairs = sample_pairs();\n    let (store, size) = build_mem(&pairs, tiny_options()).unwrap();\n    let reader = FaultyReader::new(\n        MemReader::new(store),\n        ReadFaults {\n            max_bytes_per_read: Some(7),\n            ..ReadFaults::default()\n        },\n    );\n    let table = Table::open(reader, size).unwrap();\n    table.validate().unwrap();\n    for (k, v) in pairs.iter().step_by(7) {\n        assert_eq!(table.get(k).unwrap().as_ref(), Some(v));\n    }\n    let all = collect_scan(&table, ScanOptions::default()).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(all.len(), pairs.len());\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn injected_read_error_during_footer_open_surfaces_as_io() {\n    let pairs = sample_pairs();\n    let (store, size) = build_mem(&pairs, tiny_options()).unwrap();\n    let reader = FaultyReader::new(\n        MemReader::new(store),\n        ReadFaults {\n            // The first read fetches the footer; fail it.\n            fail_read_at_call: Some(0),\n            ..ReadFaults::default()\n        },\n    );\n    let err = match Table::open(reader, size) {\n        Err(e) => e,\n        Ok(_) => panic!(\"expected injected IO error at open\"),\n    };\n    assert!(matches!(err, Error::Io(_)), \"got {err}\");\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn injected_read_error_during_get_surfaces_as_io() {\n    let pairs = sample_pairs();\n    let (store, size) = build_mem(&pairs, tiny_options()).unwrap();\n    let reader = FaultyReader::new(\n        MemReader::new(store),\n        ReadFaults {\n            // open() reads footer (1 call) + index block; fail call 2.\n            fail_read_at_call: Some(2),\n            ..ReadFaults::default()\n        },\n    );\n    // Depending on fragmentation counts the failure may land in open or get;\n    // either way it must be an IO error, never a wrong answer.\n    match Table::open(reader, size) {\n        Ok(table) => {\n            let err = table.get(b\"k/00150\").unwrap_err();\n            assert!(matches!(err, Error::Io(_)), \"got {err}\");\n        }\n        Err(Error::Io(_)) => {}\n        Err(other) => panic!(\"expected IO error, got {other}\"),\n    }\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn io_helpers_reject_impossible_counts() {\n    let store = MemStore::new();\n    let mut w = BadWriter;\n    assert!(append_all(&mut w, b\"abc\").is_err());\n\n    let mut buf = [0u8; 4];\n    let r = OverReader;\n    assert!(read_fill(&r, &mut buf, 0).is_err());\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Test-only writer wrappers\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nstruct AlwaysShort<W> {\n    inner: W,\n    max: usize,\n}\nimpl<W: psst::io::WritableFile> psst::io::WritableFile for AlwaysShort<W> {\n    fn append(&mut self, data: &[u8]) -> psst::Result<usize> {\n        let n = self.max.min(data.len()).max(1);\n        self.inner.append(&data[..n])\n    }\n    fn sync(&mut self) -> psst::Result<()> {\n        self.inner.sync()\n    }\n}\n\nstruct CountingWriter<W> {\n    inner: W,\n}\nimpl<W> CountingWriter<W> {\n    fn new(inner: W) -> Self {\n        CountingWriter { inner }\n    }\n}\nimpl<W: psst::io::WritableFile> psst::io::WritableFile for CountingWriter<W> {\n    fn append(&mut self, data: &[u8]) -> psst::Result<usize> {\n        self.inner.append(data)\n    }\n    fn sync(&mut self) -> psst::Result<()> {\n        self.inner.sync()\n    }\n}\n\nstruct BadWriter;\nimpl psst::io::WritableFile for BadWriter {\n    fn append(&mut self, _data: &[u8]) -> psst::Result<usize> {\n        Ok(0) // append_all must treat zero progress as an error\n    }\n    fn sync(&mut self) -> psst::Result<()> {\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\nstruct OverReader;\nimpl psst::io::RandomAccessFile for OverReader {\n    fn read_at(&self, buf: &mut [u8], _offset: u64) -> psst::Result<usize> {\n        Ok(buf.len() + 1) // impossible count\n    }\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":48,"oldLines":14,"newStart":48,"newLines":14,"lines":[" }"," "," #[test]","-fn injected_late_append_failure_during_finish() {","-    // Tiny blocks: appends 0.. are data blocks, and metaindex/index/footer","-    // appends come late. End-to-end HTTP verification: a real server thread on an ephemeral port,\n//! driven over raw TCP (no HTTP client dependency). Also exercises the\n//! file-backed atomic build path and corruption reporting through HTTP.\n\nuse std::io::{Read, Write};\nuse std::net::TcpStream;\nuse std::path::PathBuf;\nuse std::thread;\nuse std::time::Duration;\n\nuse psst::server::HttpServer;\n\nstruct TestServer {\n    addr: String,\n    dir: PathBuf,\n}\n\nfn spawn_server() -> TestServer {\n    let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(\n        \"psst-http-test-{}-{}\",\n        std::process::id(),\n        std::time::SystemTime::now()\n            .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)\n            .unwrap()\n            .as_nanos()\n    ));\n    let server = HttpServer::bind(dir.clone(), \"127.0.0.1:0\").unwrap();\n    let addr = server.local_addr().unwrap();\n    thread::spawn(move || {\n        let _ = server.serve();\n    });\n    let ts = TestServer { addr, dir };\n    // Wait for health.\n    for _ in 0..50 {\n        if ts.raw(\"GET\", \"/healthz\", None).is_ok() {\n            return ts;\n        }\n        thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20));\n    }\n    panic!(\"server did not come up\");\n}\n\nimpl Drop for TestServer {\n    fn drop(&mut self) {\n        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&self.dir);\n    }\n}\n\nfn http(addr: &str, method: &str, path: &str, body: Option<&str>) -> (u16, String) {\n    let mut stream = TcpStream::connect(addr).unwrap();\n    stream.set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(5))).unwrap();\n    let mut req = format!(\"{method} {path} HTTP/1.1\\r\\nHost: localhost\\r\\nConnection: close\\r\\n\");\n    if let Some(b) = body {\n        req.push_str(&format!(\"Content-Length: {}\\r\\n\", b.len()));\n    }\n    req.push_str(\"\\r\\n\");\n    if let Some(b) = body {\n        req.push_str(b);\n    }\n    stream.write_all(req.as_bytes()).unwrap();\n    let mut raw = Vec::new();\n    stream.read_to_end(&mut raw).unwrap();\n    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&raw);\n    let status: u16 = text\n        .split_whitespace()\n        .nth(1)\n        .unwrap()\n        .parse()\n        .unwrap();\n    let json = text.split_once(\"\\r\\n\\r\\n\").map(|(_, b)| b).unwrap_or(\"\");\n    (status, json.to_string())\n}\n\nimpl TestServer {\n    fn raw(&self, method: &str, path: &str, body: Option<&str>) -> std::io::Result<(u16, String)> {\n        Ok(http(&self.addr, method, path, body))\n    }\n    fn req(&self, method: &str, path: &str, body: Option<&str>) -> (u16, String) {\n        self.raw(method, path, body).unwrap()\n    }\n}\n\n/// Minimal substring assertions keep the tests independent of key ordering in\n/// JSON objects.\nfn assert_contains(haystack: &str, needle: &str) {\n    assert!(\n        haystack.contains(needle),\n        \"expected response to contain {needle:?}, got: {haystack}\"\n    );\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn full_lifecycle_over_http() {\n    let s = spawn_server();\n\n    let (code, body) = s.req(\"GET\", \"/healthz\", None);\n    assert_eq!(code, 200);\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"ok\\\":true\");\n\n    // Build a table. Keys are hex: \"\", 00, 61 (\"a\"), 62 (\"b\"), prefix-heavy.\n    let payload = concat!(\n        \"{\\\"block_size\\\":256,\\\"restart_interval\\\":4,\\\"entries\\\":[\",\n        \"[\\\"\\\",\\\"7630\\\"],[\\\"00\\\",\\\"7631\\\"],[\\\"61616130\\\",\\\"7632\\\"],[\\\"61616131\\\",\\\"7633\\\"],[\\\"6161613261\\\",\\\"7634\\\"],[\\\"6161613262\\\",\\\"7635\\\"],[\\\"7a\\\",\\\"7636\\\"]\",\n        \"]}\"\n    );\n    let (code, body) = s.req(\"PUT\", \"/tables/demo\", Some(payload));\n    assert_eq!(code, 201, \"{body}\");\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"ok\\\":true\");\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"entries\\\":7\");\n\n    // Duplicate build over an existing file is rejected (create_new).\n    let (code, _) = s.req(\"PUT\", \"/tables/demo\", Some(payload));\n    assert_eq!(code, 409);\n\n    // Point gets.\n    let (code, body) = s.req(\"GET\", \"/tables/demo/get?key=\", None);\n    assert_eq!(code, 200);\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"found\\\":true\");\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"value\\\":\\\"7630\\\"\");\n\n    let (code, body) = s.req(\"GET\", \"/tables/demo/get?key=61616131\", None);\n    assert_eq!(code, 200);\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"value\\\":\\\"7633\\\"\");\n\n    let (code, body) = s.req(\"GET\", \"/tables/demo/get?key=ff\", None);\n    assert_eq!(code, 200);\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"found\\\":false\");\n\n    // Missing key parameter is a 400.\n    let (code, _) = s.req(\"GET\", \"/tables/demo/get\", None);\n    assert_eq!(code, 400);\n\n    // Range scan across multiple blocks.\n    let (code, body) = s.req(\"GET\", \"/tables/demo/scan?start=61616130&end=7a\", None);\n    assert_eq!(code, 200);\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"count\\\":4\"); // aaa0 aaa1 aaa2a aaa2b\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"61616130\\\"\");\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"6161613262\\\"\");\n\n    // Inclusive end + limit.\n    let (code, body) = s.req(\"GET\", \"/tables/demo/scan?end=61616131&end_inclusive&limit=2\", None);\n    assert_eq!(code, 200);\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"count\\\":2\");\n\n    // Validate.\n    let (code, body) = s.req(\"POST\", \"/tables/demo/validate\", None);\n    assert_eq!(code, 200);\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"valid\\\":true\");\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"total_entries\\\":7\");\n\n    // Listing includes the table.\n    let (code, body) = s.req(\"GET\", \"/tables\", None);\n    assert_eq!(code, 200);\n    assert_contains(&body, \"demo\");\n\n    // File exists at the expected path.\n    assert!(s.dir.join(\"demo\").is_file());\n\n    // Delete and re-list.\n    let (code, body) = s.req(\"DELETE\", \"/tables/demo\", None);\n    assert_eq!(code, 200);\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"deleted\\\":\\\"demo\\\"\");\n    assert!(!s.dir.join(\"demo\").exists());\n\n    // Getting a missing table is 404.\n    let (code, _) = s.req(\"GET\", \"/tables/demo/get?key=00\", None);\n    assert_eq!(code, 404);\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn http_reports_corruption_with_400() {\n    let s = spawn_server();\n    let payload = \"{\\\"entries\\\":[[\\\"6b31\\\",\\\"7631\\\"],[\\\"6b32\\\",\\\"7632\\\"],[\\\"6b33\\\",\\\"7633\\\"],[\\\"6b34\\\",\\\"7634\\\"],[\\\"6b35\\\",\\\"7635\\\"]]}\";\n    let (code, _) = s.req(\"PUT\", \"/tables/bad\", Some(payload));\n    assert_eq!(code, 201);\n\n    // Corrupt one byte of the file on disk, then validation must fail cleanly.\n    let path = s.dir.join(\"bad\");\n    let mut bytes = std::fs::read(&path).unwrap();\n    bytes[10] ^= 0xff;\n    std::fs::write(&path, bytes).unwrap();\n\n    let (code, body) = s.req(\"POST\", \"/tables/bad/validate\", None);\n    assert_eq!(code, 400);\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"ok\\\":false\");\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"error_kind\\\":\\\"corruption\\\"\");\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn http_rejects_bad_requests() {\n    let s = spawn_server();\n\n    // Malformed JSON.\n    let (code, _) = s.req(\"PUT\", \"/tables/x\", Some(\"{not json\"));\n    assert_eq!(code, 400);\n\n    // Missing entries.\n    let (code, _) = s.req(\"PUT\", \"/tables/x\", Some(\"{}\"));\n    assert_eq!(code, 400);\n\n    // Odd-length hex key.\n    let (code, body) = s.req(\"PUT\", \"/tables/x\", Some(\"{\\\"entries\\\":[[\\\"abc\\\",\\\"\\\"]]}\"));\n    assert_eq!(code, 400);\n    assert_contains(&body, \"hex\");\n\n    // Path traversal in the table name.\n    let (code, _) = s.req(\"PUT\", \"/tables/..%2fx\", Some(\"{\\\"entries\\\":[]}\"));\n    // The router treats '/..%2fx' literally as one segment; name validation\n    // rejects the slash-free '..%2fx' only after decoding — here no decoding\n    // happens on the path, so it must at minimum not escape the directory.\n    // Accept either a 400 (invalid name char set would need %) or creation\n    // entirely inside the data dir; it must never be 2xx:\n    assert!(code == 400 || code == 404);\n\n    // Zero entries refused.\n    let (code, _) = s.req(\"PUT\", \"/tables/y\", Some(\"{\\\"entries\\\":[]}\"));\n    assert_eq!(code, 400);\n\n    // Unknown route.\n    let (code, _) = s.req(\"GET\", \"/nope\", None);\n    assert_eq!(code, 404);\n}\n"},"name":"Write","type":"tool_use"}],"id":"msg_f14c29e50bdf99110d92e134","model":"auto_model/urm","role":"assistant","stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"type":"message","usage":{"input_tokens":874,"cache_creation_input_tokens":0,"cache_read_input_tokens":144184,"output_tokens":2966,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[],"speed":"standard"},"stop_details":null},"wireToolInputs":{"call_6tusykonbonmyx2qd0ux3dzm":{"content":"//! End-to-end HTTP verification: a real server thread on an ephemeral port,\n//! driven over raw TCP (no HTTP client dependency). Also exercises the\n//! file-backed atomic build path and corruption reporting through HTTP.\n\nuse std::io::{Read, Write};\nuse std::net::TcpStream;\nuse std::path::PathBuf;\nuse std::thread;\nuse std::time::Duration;\n\nuse psst::server::HttpServer;\n\nstruct TestServer {\n    addr: String,\n    dir: PathBuf,\n}\n\nfn spawn_server() -> TestServer {\n    let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(\n        \"psst-http-test-{}-{}\",\n        std::process::id(),\n        std::time::SystemTime::now()\n            .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)\n            .unwrap()\n            .as_nanos()\n    ));\n    let server = HttpServer::bind(dir.clone(), \"127.0.0.1:0\").unwrap();\n    let addr = server.local_addr().unwrap();\n    thread::spawn(move || {\n        let _ = server.serve();\n    });\n    let ts = TestServer { addr, dir };\n    // Wait for health.\n    for _ in 0..50 {\n        if ts.raw(\"GET\", \"/healthz\", None).is_ok() {\n            return ts;\n        }\n        thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20));\n    }\n    panic!(\"server did not come up\");\n}\n\nimpl Drop for TestServer {\n    fn drop(&mut self) {\n        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&self.dir);\n    }\n}\n\nfn http(addr: &str, method: &str, path: &str, body: Option<&str>) -> (u16, String) {\n    let mut stream = TcpStream::connect(addr).unwrap();\n    stream.set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(5))).unwrap();\n    let mut req = format!(\"{method} {path} HTTP/1.1\\r\\nHost: localhost\\r\\nConnection: close\\r\\n\");\n    if let Some(b) = body {\n        req.push_str(&format!(\"Content-Length: {}\\r\\n\", b.len()));\n    }\n    req.push_str(\"\\r\\n\");\n    if let Some(b) = body {\n        req.push_str(b);\n    }\n    stream.write_all(req.as_bytes()).unwrap();\n    let mut raw = Vec::new();\n    stream.read_to_end(&mut raw).unwrap();\n    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&raw);\n    let status: u16 = text\n        .split_whitespace()\n        .nth(1)\n        .unwrap()\n        .parse()\n        .unwrap();\n    let json = text.split_once(\"\\r\\n\\r\\n\").map(|(_, b)| b).unwrap_or(\"\");\n    (status, json.to_string())\n}\n\nimpl TestServer {\n    fn raw(&self, method: &str, path: &str, body: Option<&str>) -> std::io::Result<(u16, String)> {\n        Ok(http(&self.addr, method, path, body))\n    }\n    fn req(&self, method: &str, path: &str, body: Option<&str>) -> (u16, String) {\n        self.raw(method, path, body).unwrap()\n    }\n}\n\n/// Minimal substring assertions keep the tests independent of key ordering in\n/// JSON objects.\nfn assert_contains(haystack: &str, needle: &str) {\n    assert!(\n        haystack.contains(needle),\n        \"expected response to contain {needle:?}, got: {haystack}\"\n    );\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn full_lifecycle_over_http() {\n    let s = spawn_server();\n\n    let (code, body) = s.req(\"GET\", \"/healthz\", None);\n    assert_eq!(code, 200);\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"ok\\\":true\");\n\n    // Build a table. Keys are hex: \"\", 00, 61 (\"a\"), 62 (\"b\"), prefix-heavy.\n    let payload = concat!(\n        \"{\\\"block_size\\\":256,\\\"restart_interval\\\":4,\\\"entries\\\":[\",\n        \"[\\\"\\\",\\\"7630\\\"],[\\\"00\\\",\\\"7631\\\"],[\\\"61616130\\\",\\\"7632\\\"],[\\\"61616131\\\",\\\"7633\\\"],[\\\"6161613261\\\",\\\"7634\\\"],[\\\"6161613262\\\",\\\"7635\\\"],[\\\"7a\\\",\\\"7636\\\"]\",\n        \"]}\"\n    );\n    let (code, body) = s.req(\"PUT\", \"/tables/demo\", Some(payload));\n    assert_eq!(code, 201, \"{body}\");\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"ok\\\":true\");\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"entries\\\":7\");\n\n    // Duplicate build over an existing file is rejected (create_new).\n    let (code, _) = s.req(\"PUT\", \"/tables/demo\", Some(payload));\n    assert_eq!(code, 409);\n\n    // Point gets.\n    let (code, body) = s.req(\"GET\", \"/tables/demo/get?key=\", None);\n    assert_eq!(code, 200);\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"found\\\":true\");\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"value\\\":\\\"7630\\\"\");\n\n    let (code, body) = s.req(\"GET\", \"/tables/demo/get?key=61616131\", None);\n    assert_eq!(code, 200);\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"value\\\":\\\"7633\\\"\");\n\n    let (code, body) = s.req(\"GET\", \"/tables/demo/get?key=ff\", None);\n    assert_eq!(code, 200);\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"found\\\":false\");\n\n    // Missing key parameter is a 400.\n    let (code, _) = s.req(\"GET\", \"/tables/demo/get\", None);\n    assert_eq!(code, 400);\n\n    // Range scan across multiple blocks.\n    let (code, body) = s.req(\"GET\", \"/tables/demo/scan?start=61616130&end=7a\", None);\n    assert_eq!(code, 200);\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"count\\\":4\"); // aaa0 aaa1 aaa2a aaa2b\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"61616130\\\"\");\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"6161613262\\\"\");\n\n    // Inclusive end + limit.\n    let (code, body) = s.req(\"GET\", \"/tables/demo/scan?end=61616131&end_inclusive&limit=2\", None);\n    assert_eq!(code, 200);\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"count\\\":2\");\n\n    // Validate.\n    let (code, body) = s.req(\"POST\", \"/tables/demo/validate\", None);\n    assert_eq!(code, 200);\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"valid\\\":true\");\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"total_entries\\\":7\");\n\n    // Listing includes the table.\n    let (code, body) = s.req(\"GET\", \"/tables\", None);\n    assert_eq!(code, 200);\n    assert_contains(&body, \"demo\");\n\n    // File exists at the expected path.\n    assert!(s.dir.join(\"demo\").is_file());\n\n    // Delete and re-list.\n    let (code, body) = s.req(\"DELETE\", \"/tables/demo\", None);\n    assert_eq!(code, 200);\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"deleted\\\":\\\"demo\\\"\");\n    assert!(!s.dir.join(\"demo\").exists());\n\n    // Getting a missing table is 404.\n    let (code, _) = s.req(\"GET\", \"/tables/demo/get?key=00\", None);\n    assert_eq!(code, 404);\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn http_reports_corruption_with_400() {\n    let s = spawn_server();\n    let payload = \"{\\\"entries\\\":[[\\\"6b31\\\",\\\"7631\\\"],[\\\"6b32\\\",\\\"7632\\\"],[\\\"6b33\\\",\\\"7633\\\"],[\\\"6b34\\\",\\\"7634\\\"],[\\\"6b35\\\",\\\"7635\\\"]]}\";\n    let (code, _) = s.req(\"PUT\", \"/tables/bad\", Some(payload));\n    assert_eq!(code, 201);\n\n    // Corrupt one byte of the file on disk, then validation must fail cleanly.\n    let path = s.dir.join(\"bad\");\n    let mut bytes = std::fs::read(&path).unwrap();\n    bytes[10] ^= 0xff;\n    std::fs::write(&path, bytes).unwrap();\n\n    let (code, body) = s.req(\"POST\", \"/tables/bad/validate\", None);\n    assert_eq!(code, 400);\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"ok\\\":false\");\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"error_kind\\\":\\\"corruption\\\"\");\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn http_rejects_bad_requests() {\n    let s = s.req(\"PUT\", \"/tables/x\", Some(\"{}\"));\n    assert_eq!(code, 400);\n\n    // Odd-length hex key.\n    let (code, body) = s.req(\"PUT\", \"/tables/x\", Some(\"{\\\"entries\\\":[[\\\"abc\\\",\\\"\\\"]]}\"));\n    assert_eq!(code, 400);\n    assert_contains(&body, \"hex\");\n\n    // Path traversal in the table name.\n    let (code, _) = s.req(\"PUT\", \"/tables/..%2fx\", Some(\"{\\\"entries\\\":[]}\"));\n    // The router treats '/..%2fx' literally as one segment; name validation\n    // rejects the slash-free '..%2fx' only after decoding — here no End-to-end HTTP verification: a real server thread on an ephemeral port,\n//! driven over raw TCP (no HTTP client dependency). Also exercises the\n//! file-backed atomic build path and corruption reporting through HTTP.\n\nuse std::io::{Read, Write};\nuse std::net::TcpStream;\nuse std::path::PathBuf;\nuse std::thread;\nuse std::time::Duration;\n\nuse psst::server::HttpServer;\n\nstruct TestServer {\n    addr: String,\n    dir: PathBuf,\n}\n\nfn spawn_server() -> TestServer {\n    let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(\n        \"psst-http-test-{}-{}\",\n        std::process::id(),\n        std::time::SystemTime::now()\n            .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)\n            .unwrap()\n            .as_nanos()\n    ));\n    let server = HttpServer::bind(dir.clone(), \"127.0.0.1:0\").unwrap();\n    let addr = server.local_addr().unwrap();\n    thread::spawn(move || {\n        let _ = server.serve();\n    });\n    let ts = TestServer { addr, dir };\n    // Wait for health.\n    for _ in 0..50 {\n        if ts.raw(\"GET\", \"/healthz\", None).is_ok() {\n            return ts;\n        }\n        thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20));\n    }\n    panic!(\"server did not come up\");\n}\n\nimpl Drop for TestServer {\n    fn drop(&mut self) {\n        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&self.dir);\n    }\n}\n\nfn http(addr: &str, method: &str, path: &str, body: Option<&str>) -> (u16, String) {\n    let mut stream = TcpStream::connect(addr).unwrap();\n    stream.set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(5))).unwrap();\n    let mut req = format!(\"{method} {path} HTTP/1.1\\r\\nHost: localhost\\r\\nConnection: close\\r\\n\");\n    if let Some(b) = body {\n        req.push_str(&format!(\"Content-Length: {}\\r\\n\", b.len()));\n    }\n    req.push_str(\"\\r\\n\");\n    if let Some(b) = body {\n        req.push_str(b);\n    }\n    stream.write_all(req.as_bytes()).unwrap();\n    let mut raw = Vec::new();\n    stream.read_to_end(&mut raw).unwrap();\n    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&raw);\n    let status: u16 = text\n        .split_whitespace()\n        .nth(1)\n        .unwrap()\n        .parse()\n        .unwrap();\n    let json = text.split_once(\"\\r\\n\\r\\n\").map(|(_, b)| b).unwrap_or(\"\");\n    (status, json.to_string())\n}\n\nimpl TestServer {\n    fn raw(&self, method: &str, path: &str, body: Option<&str>) -> std::io::Result<(u16, String)> {\n        Ok(http(&self.addr, method, path, body))\n    }\n    fn req(&self, method: &str, path: &str, body: Option<&str>) -> (u16, String) {\n        self.raw(method, path, body).unwrap()\n    }\n}\n\n/// Minimal substring assertions keep the tests independent of key ordering in\n/// JSON objects.\nfn assert_contains(haystack: &str, needle: &str) {\n    assert!(\n        haystack.contains(needle),\n        \"expected response to contain {needle:?}, got: {haystack}\"\n    );\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn full_lifecycle_over_http() {\n    let s = spawn_server();\n\n    let (code, body) = s.req(\"GET\", \"/healthz\", None);\n    assert_eq!(code, 200);\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"ok\\\":true\");\n\n    // Build a table. Keys are hex: \"\", 00, 61 (\"a\"), 62 (\"b\"), prefix-heavy.\n    let payload = concat!(\n        \"{\\\"block_size\\\":256,\\\"restart_interval\\\":4,\\\"entries\\\":[\",\n        \"[\\\"\\\",\\\"7630\\\"],[\\\"00\\\",\\\"7631\\\"],[\\\"61616130\\\",\\\"7632\\\"],[\\\"61616131\\\",\\\"7633\\\"],[\\\"6161613261\\\",\\\"7634\\\"],[\\\"6161613262\\\",\\\"7635\\\"],[\\\"7a\\\",\\\"7636\\\"]\",\n        \"]}\"\n    );\n    let (code, body) = s.req(\"PUT\", \"/tables/demo\", Some(payload));\n    assert_eq!(code, 201, \"{body}\");\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"ok\\\":true\");\n End-to-end HTTP verification: a real server thread on an ephemeral port,\n//! driven over raw TCP (no HTTP client dependency). Also exercises the\n//! file-backed atomic build path and corruption reporting through HTTP.\n\nuse std::io::{Read, Write};\nuse std::net::TcpStream;\nuse std::path::PathBuf;\nuse std::thread;\nuse std::time::Duration;\n\nuse psst::server::HttpServer;\n\nstruct TestServer {\n    addr: String,\n    dir: PathBuf,\n}\n\nfn spawn_server() -> TestServer {\n    let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(\n        \"psst-http-test-{}-{}\",\n        std::process::id(),\n        std::time::SystemTime::now()\n            .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)\n            .unwrap()\n            .as_nanos()\n    ));\n    let server = HttpServer::bind(dir.clone(), \"127.0.0.1:0\").unwrap();\n    let addr = server.local_addr().unwrap();\n    thread::spawn(move || {\n        let _ = server.serve();\n    });\n    let ts = TestServer { addr, dir };\n    // Wait for health.\n    for _ in 0..50 {\n        if ts.raw(\"GET\", \"/healthz\", None).is_ok() {\n            return ts;\n        }\n        thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20));\n    }\n    panic!(\"server did not come up\");\n}\n\nimpl Drop for TestServer {\n    fn drop(&mut self) {\n        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&self.dir);\n    }\n}\n\nfn http(addr: &str, method: &str, path: &str, body: Option<&str>) -> (u16, String) {\n    let mut stream = TcpStream::connect(addr).unwrap();\n    stream.set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(5))).unwrap();\n    let mut req = format!(\"{method} {path} HTTP/1.1\\r\\nHost: localhost\\r\\nConnection: close\\r\\n\");\n    if let Some(b) = body {\n        req.push_str(&format!(\"Content-Length: {}\\r\\n\", b.len()));\n    }\n    req.push_str(\"\\r\\n\");\n    if let Some(b) = body {\n        req.push_str(b);\n    }\n    stream.write_all(req.as_bytes()).unwrap();\n    let mut raw = Vec::new();\n    stream.read_to_end(&mut raw).unwrap();\n    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&raw);\n    let status: u16 = text\n        .split_whitespace()\n        .nth(1)\n        .unwrap()\n        .parse()\n        .unwrap();\n    let json = text.split_once(\"\\r\\n\\r\\n\").map(|(_, b)| b).unwrap_or(\"\");\n    (status, json.to_string())\n}\n\nimpl TestServer {\n    fn raw(&self, method: &str, path: &str, body: Option<&str>) -> std::io::Result<(u16, String)> {\n        Ok(http(&self.addr, method, path, body))\n    }\n    fn req(&self, method: &str, path: &str, body: Option<&str>) -> (u16, String) {\n        self.raw(method, path, body).unwrap()\n    }\n}\n\n/// Minimal substring assertions keep the tests independent of key ordering in\n/// JSON objects.\nfn assert_contains(haystack: &str, needle: &str) {\n    assert!(\n        haystack.contains(needle),\n        \"expected response to contain {needle:?}, got: {haystack}\"\n    );\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn full_lifecycle_over_http() {\n    let s = spawn_server();\n\n    let (code, body) = s.req(\"GET\", \"/healthz\", None);\n    assert_eq!(code, 200);\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"ok\\\":true\");\n\n    // Build a table. Keys are hex: \"\", 00, 61 (\"a\"), 62 (\"b\"), prefix-heavy.\n    let payload = concat!(\n        \"{\\\"block_size\\\":256,\\\"restart_interval\\\":4,\\\"entries\\\":[\",\n        \"[\\\"\\\",\\\"7630\\\"],[\\\"00\\\",\\\"7631\\\"],[\\\"61616130\\\",\\\"7632\\\"],[\\\"61616131\\\",\\\"7633\\\"],[\\\"6161613261\\\",\\\"7634\\\"],[\\\"6161613262\\\",\\\"7635\\\"],[\\\"7a\\\",\\\"7636\\\"]\",\n        \"]}\"\n    );\n    let (code, body) = s.req(\"PUT\", \"/tables/demo\", Some(payload));\n    assert_eq!(code, 201, \"{body}\");\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"ok\\\":true\");\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"entries\\\":7\");\n\n    // Duplicate build over an existing file is rejected (create_new).\n    let (code, _) = s.req(\"PUT\", \"/tables/demo\", Some(payload));\n    assert_eq!(code, 409);\n\n    // Point gets.\n    let (code, body) = s.req(\"GET\", \"/tables/demo/get?key=\", None);\n    assert_eq!(code, 200);\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"found\\\":true\");\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"value\\\":\\\"7630\\\"\");\n\n    let (code, body) = s.req(\"GET\", \"/tables/demo/get?key=61616131\", None);\n    assert_eq!(code, 200);\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"value\\\":\\\"7633\\\"\");\n\n    let (code, body) = s.req(\"GET\", \"/tables/demo/get?key=ff\", None);\n    assert_eq!(code, 200);\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"found\\\":false\");\n\n    // Missing key parameter is a 400.\n    let (code, _) = s.req(\"GET\", \"/tables/demo/get\", None);\n    assert_eq!(code, 400);\n\n    // Range scan across multiple blocks.\n    let (code, body) = s.req(\"GET\", \"/tables/demo/scan?start=61616130&end=7a\", None);\n    assert_eq!(code, 200);\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"count\\\":4\"); // aaa0 aaa1 aaa2a aaa2b\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"61616130\\\"\");\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"6161613262\\\"\");\n\n    // Inclusive end + limit.\n    let (code, body) = s.req(\"GET\", \"/tables/demo/scan?end=61616131&end_inclusive&limit=2\", None);\n    assert_eq!(code, 200);\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"count\\\":2\");\n\n    // Validate.\n    let (code, body) = s.req(\"POST\", \"/tables/demo/validate\", None);\n    assert_eq!(code, 200);\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"valid\\\":true\");\n    assert_contains(&body, \"\\\"total_entries\\\":7\");\n\n    // Listing includes the table.\n    let (code, body) = s.req(\"GET\", \"/tables\", None);\n    assert_eq!(code, 200);\n    assert_contains(&body, \"demo\");\n\n    // File exists at the expected path.\n (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"uuid":"0da0be4b-989d-49fb-ac64-f33fe52a171d","timestamp":"2026-09-23T02:29:34.424Z","toolUseResult":{"filePath":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp8/b/tests/io_faults.rs","oldString":"    let store = MemStore::new();\n    let mut w = BadWriter;\n    assert!(append_all(&mut w, b\"abc\").is_err());","newString":"    let mut w = BadWriter;\n    assert!(append_all(&mut w, b\"abc\").is_err());","originalFile":"//! Injectable I/O layer: injected write/read faults surface as `Error::Io`,\n//! the storage layer retries partial writes and fragmented reads, and the\n//! durability boundary (`sync`) is exercised explicitly.\n\nmod common;\n\nuse common::*;\nuse psst::error::Error;\nuse psst::io::{\n    append_all, read_fill, FaultyReader, FaultyWriter, MemReader, MemStore,\n    MemWriter, ReadFaults, WriteFaults,\n};\nuse psst::table::{collect_scan, Options, ScanOptions, Table, TableBuilder};\n\nfn sample_pairs() -> Vec<(Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>)> {\n    (0..300u32)\n        .map(|i| (format!(\"k/{i:04}\").into_bytes(), format!(\"v{i}\").into_bytes()))\n        .collect()\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn injected_append_failure_aborts_build_and_leaves_no_success() {\n    let pairs = sample_pairs();\n    let store = MemStore::new();\n    let writer = FaultyWriter::new(\n        MemWriter::new(store.clone()),\n        WriteFaults {\n            // The very first data block append fails.\n            fail_append_at: Some(0),\n            ..WriteFaults::default()\n        },\n    );\n    let mut builder = TableBuilder::new(writer, Options::default()).unwrap();\n    let mut failed = false;\n    for (k, v) in &pairs {\n        if builder.add(k, v).is_err() {\n            failed = true;\n            break;\n        }\n    }\n    if !failed {\n        let err = builder.finish().unwrap_err();\n        assert!(matches!(err, Error::Io(_)), \"got {err}\");\n    }\n    // Whatever partial bytes exist must not parse as a table.\n    let open = Table::open(MemReader::new(store.clone()), store.len() as u64);\n    assert!(matches!(open, Err(Error::Io(_)) | Err(Error::Corruption(_))));\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn injected_late_append_failure_aborts_build() {\n    // Tiny blocks produce many append calls; a high call index lands deep in\n    // the build (possibly in finish), and wherever it lands it must surface as\n    // an IO error rather than a corrupt-but-accepted file.\n    let pairs = sample_pairs();\n    let store = MemStore::new();\n    let writer = FaultyWriter::new(\n        MemWriter::new(store.clone()),\n        WriteFaults {\n            fail_append_at: Some(40),\n            ..WriteFaults::default()\n        },\n    );\n    let mut builder = TableBuilder::new(\n        writer,\n        Options {\n            block_size: 64,\n            restart_interval: 4,\n        },\n    )\n    .unwrap();\n\n    let mut failed = false;\n    for (k, v) in &pairs {\n        if builder.add(k, v).is_err() {\n            failed = true;\n            break;\n        }\n    }\n    if !failed {\n        let err = builder.finish().unwrap_err();\n        assert!(matches!(err, Error::Io(_)), \"finish error: {err}\");\n    }\n\n    let open = Table::open(MemReader::new(store.clone()), store.len() as u64);\n    assert!(matches!(open, Err(Error::Io(_)) | Err(Error::Corruption(_))));\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn injected_sync_failure_propagates_from_finish() {\n    let pairs = sample_pairs();\n    let store = MemStore::new();\n    let writer = FaultyWriter::new(\n        MemWriter::new(store),\n        WriteFaults {\n            fail_sync_at: Some(0),\n            ..WriteFaults::default()\n        },\n    );\n    let mut builder = TableBuilder::new(writer, Options::default()).unwrap();\n    for (k, v) in &pairs {\n        builder.add(k, v).unwrap();\n    }\n    let err = builder.finish().unwrap_err();\n    assert!(matches!(err, Error::Io(_)), \"sync error: {err}\");\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn short_writes_are_retried_and_file_is_byte_identical() {\n    let pairs = sample_pairs();\n    let (good_store, size) = build_mem(&pairs, tiny_options()).unwrap();\n\n    // Every append accepts at most 3 bytes; the builder's retry loop must\n    // produce a byte-identical file.\n    let faulty_store = MemStore::new();\n    let writer = AlwaysShort {\n        inner: MemWriter::new(faulty_store.clone()),\n        max: 3,\n    };\n    let mut builder = TableBuilder::new(writer, tiny_options()).unwrap();\n    for (k, v) in &pairs {\n        builder.add(k, v).unwrap();\n    }\n    let stats = builder.finish().unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(stats.bytes, size);\n    assert_eq!(faulty_store.snapshot(), good_store.snapshot());\n\n    // And the resulting table reads correctly.\n    let table = Table::open(MemReader::new(faulty_store.clone()), size).unwrap();\n    table.validate().unwrap();\n    let all = collect_scan(&table, ScanOptions::default()).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(all.len(), pairs.len());\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn fragmented_reads_still_produce_correct_results() {\n    let pairs = sample_pairs();\n    let (store, size) = build_mem(&pairs, tiny_options()).unwrap();\n    let reader = FaultyReader::new(\n        MemReader::new(store),\n        ReadFaults {\n            max_bytes_per_read: Some(7),\n            ..ReadFaults::default()\n        },\n    );\n    let table = Table::open(reader, size).unwrap();\n    table.validate().unwrap();\n    for (k, v) in pairs.iter().step_by(7) {\n        assert_eq!(table.get(k).unwrap().as_ref(), Some(v));\n    }\n    let all = collect_scan(&table, ScanOptions::default()).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(all.len(), pairs.len());\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn injected_read_error_during_footer_open_surfaces_as_io() {\n    let pairs = sample_pairs();\n    let (store, size) = build_mem(&pairs, tiny_options()).unwrap();\n    let reader = FaultyReader::new(\n        MemReader::new(store),\n        ReadFaults {\n            // The first read fetches the footer; fail it.\n            fail_read_at_call: Some(0),\n            ..ReadFaults::default()\n        },\n    );\n    let err = match Table::open(reader, size) {\n        Err(e) => e,\n        Ok(_) => panic!(\"expected injected IO error at open\"),\n    };\n    assert!(matches!(err, Error::Io(_)), \"got {err}\");\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn injected_read_error_during_get_surfaces_as_io() {\n    let pairs = sample_pairs();\n    let (store, size) = build_mem(&pairs, tiny_options()).unwrap();\n    let reader = FaultyReader::new(\n        MemReader::new(store),\n        ReadFaults {\n            // open() reads footer (1 call) + index block; fail call 2.\n            fail_read_at_call: Some(2),\n            ..ReadFaults::default()\n        },\n    );\n    // Depending on fragmentation counts the failure may land in open or get;\n    // either way it must be an IO error, never a wrong answer.\n    match Table::open(reader, size) {\n        Ok(table) => {\n            let err = table.get(b\"k/00150\").unwrap_err();\n            assert!(matches!(err, Error::Io(_)), \"got {err}\");\n        }\n        Err(Error::Io(_)) => {}\n        Err(other) => panic!(\"expected IO error, got {other}\"),\n    }\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn io_helpers_reject_impossible_counts() {\n    let store = MemStore::new();\n    let mut w = BadWriter;\n    assert!(append_all(&mut w, b\"abc\").is_err());\n\n    let mut buf = [0u8; 4];\n    let r = OverReader;\n    assert!(read_fill(&r, &mut buf, 0).is_err());\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Test-only writer wrappers\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nstruct AlwaysShort<W> {\n    inner: W,\n    max: usize,\n}\nimpl<W: psst::io::WritableFile> psst::io::WritableFile for AlwaysShort<W> {\n    fn append(&mut self, data: &[u8]) -> psst::Result<usize> {\n        let n = self.max.min(data.len()).max(1);\n        self.inner.append(&data[..n])\n    }\n    fn sync(&mut self) -> psst::Result<()> {\n        self.inner.sync()\n    }\n}\n\nstruct BadWriter;\nimpl psst::io::WritableFile for BadWriter {\n    fn append(&mut self, _data: &[u8]) -> psst::Result<usize> {\n        Ok(0) // append_all must treat zero progress as an error\n    }\n    fn sync(&mut self) -> psst::Result<()> {\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\nstruct OverReader;\nimpl psst::io::RandomAccessFile for OverReader {\n    fn read_at(&self, buf: &mut [u8], _offset: u64) -> psst::Result<usize> {\n        Ok(buf.len() + 1) // impossible count\n    }\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":197,"oldLines":7,"newStart":197,"newLines":6,"lines":[" "," #[test]"," fn io_helpers_reject_impossible_counts() {","-    let store = MemStore::new();","     let mut w = BadWriter;","     assert!(append_all(&mut w, b\"abc\").is_err());"," "]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"8dd44886-bd05-4291-bcf8-dee3333ad4d9","session_id":"778f00cf-4c07-4d49-9d5a-e2a66c2ee10d","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp8/b","sessionId":"778f00cf-4c07-4d49-9d5a-e2a66c2ee10d","version":"2.1.280","gitBranch":"ab/run-20260922T151547Z/opp8-b","slug":"cuddly-puzzling-goblet"}

  build_table_sorted, collect_scan, Bound, Options, ScanOptions, Table,\n};\n\nfn unique_dir(tag: &str) -> std::path::PathBuf {\n    let p = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(\n        \"psst-file-test-{tag}-{}-{}\",\n        std::process::id(),\n        std::time::SystemTime::now()\n            .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)\n            .unwrap()\n            .as_nanos()\n    ));\n    std::fs::create_dir_all(&p).unwrap();\n    p\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn atomic_build_rename_and_reopen() {\n    let dir = unique_dir(\"atomic\");\n    let entries = vec![\n        (vec![1u8, 2, 3], b\"v1\".to_vec()),\n        (vec![1, 2, 4], b\"v2\".to_vec()),\n        (vec![9], b\"v3\".to_vec()),\n    ];\n    let stats =\n        build_table_sorted(&dir, \"t1\", &entries, Options::default(), 1).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(stats.entries, 3);\n    assert_eq!(stats.data_blocks, 1);\n\n    // No leftover temp files.\n    let leftovers: Vec<_> = std::fs::read_dir(&dir)\n        .unwrap()\n        .filter_map(|e| e.ok())\n        .filter(|e| e.file_name().to_string_lossy().starts_with('.'))\n        .collect();\n    assert!(leftovers.is_empty(), \"temp files left behind: {leftovers:?}\");\n\n assert_eq!(table.get(&[9]).unwrap(), Some(b\"v3\".to_vec()));\n    assert_eq!(table.get(&[0]).unwrap(), None);\n\n    std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn build_sorts_unsorted_input_and_rejects_duplicates() {\n    let dir = unique_dir(\"sort\");\n    let entries = vec![\n        (b\"c\".to_vec(), b\"3\".to_vec()),\n        (b\"a\".to_vec(), b\"1\".to_vec()),\n        (b\"b\".to_vec(), b\"2\".to_vec()),\n    ];\n    build_table_sorted(&dir, \"s\", &entries, Options::default(), 7).unwrap();\n    let table = Table::open_path(&dir.join(\"s\")).unwrap();\n    let got = collect_scan(&table, ScanOptions::default()).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(\n        got,\n        vec![\n            (b\"a\".to_vec(), std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn duplicate_table_name_is_conflict_and_temp_is_cleaned() {\n    let dir = unique_dir(\"dup\");\n    let entries = vec![(b\"k\".to_vec(), b\"v\".to_vec())];\n    build_table_sorted(&dir, \"once\", &entries, Options::default(), 1).unwrap();\n    let err = build_table_sorted(&dir, \"once\", &entries, Options::default(), 2)\n
